events.title: Andreas Klein
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: German Pianist Andreas Klein has distinguished himself as a dynamic and compelling performer with his command of a wide range of tonal colors and imaginative interpretations. The New York Times declared him “A fascinating artist with all the indispensable qualities: temperament, taste, touch, tone, the four T’s of pianism” and “A pianist who makes silences sound like music”. Andreas Klein’s career as orchestra soloist and recitalist has taken him to the world’s most prestigious venues from London’s Wigmore Hall, Berlin’s Philharmonic Hall, New York’s Carnegie Hall and Alice Tully Hall, to Washington, DC’s Kennedy Center and National Gallery. In Europe as well as in the USA, Mexico, and the Middle East, he has gained critical acclaim for his performances in major cities such as Berlin, Rome, Milan, Bern, Leipzig, Dresden, New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Washington, DC, Cleveland, Damascus, Mexico City, Calgary, and the Ravinia Festival in Chicago.

events.title: The Seven Wonders A Tribute to Fleetwood Mac
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: The Seven Wonders are world-class musicians paying homage to the music of Fleetwood Mac and Stevie Nicks. Named after the Fleetwood Mac song “Seven Wonders,” the band’s collective performing experience brings the crowd powerful renditions of these timeless tunes. They authentically recreate all the great hits of Fleetwood Mac, including Dreams, Go Your Own Way, Rhiannon, Edge of Seventeen, Landslide, Gypsy, and more. The Seven Wonders’ onstage passion reconnects fans with the music they love. Since the Seven Wonders’ inception in 2017, they have garnered national attention for their high energy performances. The Seven Wonders reconnect fans with the music they love. The Seven Wonders’ Teegan Ward commands the stage, channeling the vibrant energy of the youthful prime of Fleetwood Mac’s Stevie Knicks, the driving force behind many of Fleetwood Mac’s most iconic tracks. Ward is the consummate lead on stage, projecting her talent over star-struck audiences. With her world-class voice, incredible presence and high-intensity performance, Ward brings a show that truly inspires.

events.title: Reif Theater Arts Production of Disney’s Aladdin JR.
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Welcome to Agrabah, City of Enchantment, where every beggar has a story and every camel has a tail! Aladdin and his three friends, Babkak, Omar, and Kassim, are down on their luck until Aladdin discovers a magic lamp and the Genie who has the power to grant three wishes. Wanting to earn the respect of the princess, Jasmine, Aladdin embarks on an adventure that will test his will and his moral character. With expanded characters, new songs, and more thrills, this new adaptation of the beloved story will open up “a whole new world” to audiences of all ages! Based on the Tony Award®-winning Broadway musical, audiences’ spirits will soar with excitement over magic, mayhem, flying carpet rides, and songs from the Academy Award®-winning score. Music by Alan Menken Lyrics by Howard Ashman, Tim Rice, Chad Beguelin Book by Chad Beguelin Disney’s Aladdin JR. is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI).

events.title: The Book of Bublé – Christmas
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: “The Book of Bublé – Christmas” is a high-octane holiday tribute to style, swagger, and swing. Emmy® winner Shaun Johnson and his seven-piece band deliver Michael Bublé’s biggest hits with powerhouse vocals and bold new orchestrations—from “Haven’t Met You Yet” to “Feeling Good,” and “Frosty the Snowman” to “It’s Beginning to Look a Lot Like Christmas.” Drawing on more than two decades of national touring, Shaun, longtime frontman of Tonic Sol-fa and an artist with a recent Top 5 Billboard brings both a vocalist’s and bandleader’s perspective to the repertoire, balancing high-energy performances with the familiar songs that define the season. Musicianship and ensemble work remain at the core, keeping the show fresh and fully in the moment. Backed by a seasoned seven-piece ensemble, The Book of Bublé channels the playful, confident style that earned Shaun multiple Entertainer of the Year nominations – a holiday concert that swings.

events.title: Rock & Roll Xmas Spectacular
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Rock & Roll Xmas Spectacular is a Las Vegas-caliber, multimedia, full-production show that mixes an 8-piece band with music, comedy, parodies and even a game show! Join an all-star cast of musicians as they rock their way through timeless holiday classics and bring new takes on hit songs you didn’t even know were holiday classics. The line-up of musicians is truly legendary as Paul “Stretch” Diethelm and Ted Manderfeld are joined on stage by vocalists Pamela McNeill, Stacy Bauer, and Tim Haussner, and backed by bassist Mike Zeleny, saxophonist and flutist Mike Kreitzer and drummer Billy Thommes. You’ll hear Christmas standards like Silent Night, God Rest Ye Merry Gentlemen, Rockin’ Round the Christmas Tree, The Little Drummer Boy and many more like you’ve never heard them performed before! This event is not eligible for any discounts.

events.title: Itasca Symphony: Family Christmas with The Snowman
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: The Snowman is back at the Reif with the Itasca Symphony Orchestra for a second December, on its way to becoming a Grand Rapids tradition. The 1982 animated film, based on Raymond Briggs’ picture book, has no dialogue. A boy builds a snowman, the snowman comes to life, and together they fly off into the night sky to “Walking in the Air.” Howard Blake’s music tells the whole story, and the Itasca Symphony Orchestra plays it live while the film fills the big screen. The rest of the afternoon is holiday music for the whole family. Bring the kids and the grandparents, and make it part of your December.

events.title: Reif Cozy Concert: Sarah Morris
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Sarah Morris has a habit of missing the forest. From the day the Minneapolis-based singer-songwriter picked up a guitar, armed with the bone-deep memory of her parents’ well-loved record collection and rooted in the storytelling fire of a Mary Chapin Carpenter tune, she’s been too busy crafting love letters to the details of the trees. Sarah’s endearingly honest, expertly penned songs encourage audiences to pull away from the big picture and get caught up in the magic of our everyday minutia, the rainy day ache in her sunlit voice granting us permission to escape into stories at once hauntingly familiar and uniquely her own.

events.title: Takin’ It to the Limit: An Eagles Tribute with Collective Unconscious and the Fabulous Armadillos
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Now in the 13th incredible year of performing hundreds of sellout performances, The Fabulous Armadillos and Collective Unconscious come together to recreate the magical songs we all know as the premier band of California Rock in the 70’s, known as the Eagles. You will hear all the hits and relive the sound of your turntable spinning all those incredible albums. Hear Take It Easy, Lyin’ Eyes, One Of These Nights, Desperado, I Can’t Tell You Why, Witchy Woman, Hotel California, Take It To The Limit, and so many more! Sit back and close your eyes and bask in the joy of the Eagles live with the Fabulous Armadillos and Collective Unconscious Eagles Tribute – “Takin’ It To The Limit.”

events.title: The Ok Factor
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Olivia Diercks and Karla Peters – cellist and violinist of the new-classical crossover duo, The OK Factor – have one word to describe their musical connection: lucky. The almost telepathic way they respond to one another is palpable to the audiences they capture during performances, as is their spontaneity and joy. Organic and genuine, their original compositions and arrangements feel both comfortingly familiar and uniquely fresh, and have been described as “genre-bending” (Julie Amacher, MPR) and “pure magic” (Wausau Pilot & Review). In their 10+ years of writing, performing, and touring, The OK Factor has honed the ways they impact communities outside the concert hall. Residency work has become a deep passion – sharing intimate performances, conducting outreach activities, and leading workshops for students through their education initiative, ATLAS. Olivia and Karla are also sought-after collaborators and composers-in-residence, having worked with many regional, national, and international artists, and various digital music libraries.

events.title: Itasca Symphony: Sam Miltich with the Itasca Orchestra
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Grand Rapids’ own Sam Miltich joined the Hot Club of San Francisco as a teenager and has since toured internationally and played Lincoln Center. This February he brings his band home to share the Reif stage with the Itasca Symphony Orchestra: Sam on guitar, his father Matthew Miltich on bass, plus other instruments. The music travels. Choro (SHOH-roo) is the quick, bright instrumental music of Rio de Janeiro. The Nuevo Tango from Argentina. Čoček (CHO-chek) is the Romani dance music of the Balkans. And Sam got his start in the swinging guitar jazz Django Reinhardt made famous in 1930s Paris. For the finale, young string players from IOSP’s programs in Grand Rapids, Bigfork, and Remer join the band and the orchestra for one big celebration of music. It’s a February night out of the cold, with musicians of every age on one stage.

events.title: Guys On Ice – An Ice Fishing Musical
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: The show follows two lifelong pals, Marvin and Lloyd, as they spend a day in their ice shanty doing everything but catching fish. More than just a play, Guys on Ice is a musical tribute to the stubborn resilience of Midwesterners. Featuring show-stopping numbers like “De Wishing Hole,” “Fish is de Miracle Food,” and the legendary “Ode to a Snowmobile Suit” (featuring a zipper dance routine you have to see to believe), this production captures the heart, the humor, and the “oh-fer-cute” charm of life on the ice.

events.title: Deuces Wild – Dueling Pianos 25th Anniversary Tour
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: There are dueling piano shows...and then there is DEUCES WILD! They are unparalleled in their field and you are in for an incredible night of fun with these two amazing showmen! It is a clap along, sing along musical comedy show where the audience is always a part of the action! No one does it better than Dave and Ted. For a pair of self-taught pianists from Minnesota, David Eichholz and Ted Manderfeld have mastered the sophisticated nuances of burlesque’s best ribald and bawdy traditions. Deuces Wild! Dueling Pianos offers a Las Vegas-style show of comedy and extensive audience participation featuring an unlikely and surprising mix of music and parodies that range from classic rock and country to rap and show tunes. The key to their marathon of musical comedy, however, is the unabashed and completely liberated participation of audience members from 18 to 80. This event is not eligible for any discounts.

events.title: Dino-Light
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Dino-Light was the recipient of the prestigious Jim Henson Foundation Grant and the first feature-length theatrical production created and performed by Lightwire. In this original storyline, a famous scientist with magic powers brings a friendly dinosaur to life. When the dinosaur wanders away from home, he discovers a wonderful world full of creatures that light up the darkness and help him find the true meaning of love. This glow-in-the-dark adventure is visually amazing and has been praised for its cutting-edge blend of puppetry, technology, and dance by audiences all over the world.

events.title: Reif Cozy Concert: Adam Moe
events.description: Adam Moe is a fiddler and singer/songwriter based in Duluth, MN. In 2012, he started the folky-tonk duo Pushing Chain with a former musical partner. For the next eight years, Pushing Chain toured the US and Canada, playing venues big and small and gaining fans the old-fashioned way — face to face, one at a time. Adam has been featured on radio and television, and played some of the biggest festivals in the country, including the 2019 Woody Guthrie Festival and the 2019 Kerrville Folk Festival.

events.title: “OUR HOUSE” a Tribute to the Music of Crosby, Stills, Nash, and Young
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: “OUR HOUSE” IS A TRIBUTE TO THE MUSIC OF CROSBY, STILLS, NASH & YOUNG committed to igniting the spirit and legacy of one of music’s most emblematic ensembles. With precise musical craftsmanship and a heartfelt embrace of the CSNY storytelling ethos, our aim is to celebrate and uphold the music that resonated through their work. Our concerts are more than a tribute; they serve as an ode to the lives and ingenious artistry of Crosby, Stills, Nash, and Young, inviting fans from every generation to commemorate the indelible mark these musicians left on both the industry and the world.

events.title: Reif Theater Arts Presents: Trolls The Musical JR
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Trolls JR. is based on the irreverent DreamWorks Animation movie franchise and features a colorful, wondrous world populated by hilariously unforgettable characters. The show follows the overly optimistic Trolls, constantly with a song on their lips, and the comically pessimistic Bergens, who are only happy when they have Trolls in their stomach. The Troll thespians in Poppy’s company live by their motto: the show must go on. But when a tyrannical foreign emissary arrives in Bergenland, expectations are raised, forcing the Trolls to totally rework their show or risk being served up in the name of diplomacy by a Chef rehired and out for revenge. Based on the DreamWorks Animation Motion Picture In association with Universal Theatrical Group Book & Lyrics by Krista Knight Original Music & Lyrics by Joriah Kwamé Trolls The Musical JR. is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

events.title: Mo Pitney Trio
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Curb Records recording artist Mo Pitney received a standing ovation the very first time he performed on the iconic Grand Ole Opry stage. Named an “Artist To Watch” by Rolling Stone, Billboard and The Bobby Bones Show, Pitney has amassed over 40 million streams since the release of his autobiographical debut, Behind This Guitar. The Illinois-native leans on the influences of traditional country stalwarts like Ray Price, Buck Owens, Roger Miller and Merle Haggard. His original song, “Ain’t Bad for a Good Ol’ Boy,” was featured on The Ranch (A Netflix Original Series Official Soundtrack). Next up for Pitney, “Wake Up And Smell The Country (with Jake Worthington),” released on March 27, 2026.

events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description: Minnesota troubadour Mason Jennings returns performing old favorites and work from his new album “Dark Wings.” “I love song craft,” says Mason Jennings, a folksinger who has spent over two decades honing his craft both on stage and in the studio. “A song is like a boat on the water, and you’re trying to make it float with as few pieces as possible. If you do it right, a song can be very healing.” For Jennings, songwriting has always been about a personal connection, both with his audience and himself. He’s known for an unpretentious, emotive approach to folk music, combining introspective lyrics with acoustic melodies. His work has drawn comparisons to genre greats, including Nick Drake, John Fahey, and Tom Waits. But Jennings’ sound is distinctly his own, one that blends vulnerability with strength, simplicity with complexity. That style comes through on his new record: “Dark Wings.” His 18th studio album, the record finds Jennings moving between raw honesty about childhood scars, dark thoughts, spiritual questioning and a stubborn belief in the power of love.

events.title: Iron Range Night
events.description: The Iron Range Rocks! Celebrate the music from Minnesota’s Iron Range with performances from The Brothers Burn Mountain, Hobo Revival and The Sectionals beginning at 7 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 28. Guitar and drum duo Ryan and Jesse Dermody have been performing as The Brothers Burn Mountain for 25 years. Based out of their off-the-grid, self-constructed studio near Cotton, the duo has toured relentlessly around the midwest for more than two decades. The Brothers Burn Mountain have released 11 full-length albums of original music and released a “best of” collection in 2025. Hobo Revival, based out of Nashauk, has been performing their straight-ahead brand of rock and roll across northern Minnesota for 15 years. Led by singer-songwriter Kim Nagler, the group released its latest album “The Pulled Pork Sessions” in 2024. The Sectionals are a vocal octet performing classic jazz and modern acapella favorites. The ensemble features members from throughout the Iron Range. This event is made possible in part by a grant from the Arrowhead Regional Arts Council with funds appropriated from the Minnesota Legislature from its General Fund.

events.title: The New Standards Holiday Show
events.description: The New Standards Holiday Show has wowed Twin Cities audiences for years. The group will bring its merriment machine to the Sacred Heart Music Center altar stage for the first time at 7:30 pm Thursday, Dec. 10. The New Standards Holiday Show features the trio as wise-cracking hosts of a seasonal spectacle that’s just “Christmasy” enough. With a little help from their friends, The New Standards warms the hearts of the grinchiest of grinches in what has become an enduring, and endearing, Minnesota holiday tradition. The New Standards are Chan Poling on piano, John Munson on bass and Steve Roehm on vibraphone. events.description: Celebrate the holidays bluegrass-style. Minnesota bluegrass songstress Becky Schlegel performs Christmas classics with The High 48s at 7 pm Saturday Dec. 12. events.title: The Last Revel
events.description: Minneapolis-based The Last Revel brings its exciting Americana-folk sound to the beautiful Sacred Heart altar stage at 7:30 pm Thursday, Jan. 14. Duluth-based eerie-folk quintet Superior Siren opens. Formed in 2011, The Last Revel uses traditional folk-minded three part harmonies with honest and meaningful lyrics to deliver a passionate and soul stirring performance. Their latest, “Gone For Good,” was produced by Dave Simonett of Trampled by Turtles. events.title: 38 Special
events.description: With special guest Goldy LockS Band Thursday, November 5, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Pepper Entertainment Tickets on sale now! ABOUT 38 SPECIAL Formed in 1974, the band toured tirelessly from the start, sharpening the explosive live show that’s been 38 Special’s calling card for a half-century. Along the way, the Florida natives fine-tuned their sound too: a blend of muscle and melody, filled with the arena-rock pop hooks that would soon become staples of FM radio. Years passed... trends changed... some band members retired from the rigors... but 38 Special remained, hitting the road year after year, flying the flag for an enduring form of classic rock & roll that never dies. As 38 Special enters its sixth decade together, the music continues with Milestone. It’s the band’s first studio album in more than 20 years, and it showcases a group of road warriors with plenty of miles left in the tank. Fueled up on snarling guitars, anthemic melodies, and the desire to break new ground, they update their sound for the 2020s, bridging the gap between past and present without forgetting their rock & roll roots.

events.title: Chamber Music Up North – Sangam: Where East Meets West
events.venue: Spirit of the Lake Community Arts
events.description: 2026 edition of the annual Chamber Music Up North series presents SANGAM, a performance featuring works that are heavily influenced by Indian classical music and features compositions by Juhi Bansal, Asha Srinivasan, Reena Esmail, Nina Shekhar and Shruthi Rajasekar. The word SANGAM derived from Sanskrit and translates to “confluence” referring to a combination of Western and Indian classical music idioms. Audience members will learn about the basic elements of Indian classical music, such as raga and tala, and will be able to experience how these ancient forms are used in contemporary classical music. The concert will include non-traditional seating and stage set up for the performers and a short Meet&Greet with musicians following the performance. Performers include TCCC Artistic Director cellist Magdalena Sas and guest artists: flutist Paula Gudmundson (Professor of Music at University of Minnesota Duluth and McKnight Fellow), violist Laila Zakzook ( Isaura String Quartet), and double bassist Rolf Erdahl ( Professor of Bass at Gustavus Adolphus College).

events.title: Gary Owen
events.description: No Hard Feelings Tour Tickets on Sale Now! ABOUT GARY OWEN Gary Owen has been entertaining audiences for more than two decades with his sharp observational humor and fearless storytelling. Known for his unapologetic, rule-defying style, his material draws from his personal life, time in the military and the everyday absurdities that connect people across backgrounds. With a fanbase that has grown by the millions in recent months and continues to surge across social media, Owen’s reach has cemented his place as one of the most in-demand touring comedians today. Beyond stand-up, Owen has appeared in a wide range of feature films including BACK ON THE STRIP with Tiffany Haddish and Wesley Snipes, MEET THE BLACKS and its sequel THE HOUSE NEXT DOOR, THINK LIKE A MAN and THINK LIKE A MAN TOO, RIDE ALONG with Ice Cube and Kevin Hart, LITTLE MAN opposite the Wayans Brothers, and DADDY DAY CARE with Eddie Murphy. He is also widely recognized for his scene-stealing role as “Bearcat” in the MGM film COLLEGE. On television, Owen starred in his own BET series THE GARY OWEN SHOW and co-hosted TruTV’s sketch series UPLOAD WITH SHAQUILLE O’NEAL.

events.title: An Evening With Neil deGrasse Tyson
events.description: An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I Presented by Roberts Group Tickets on sale now! “An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I” From Star Wars to Armageddon to Titanic to The Martian to oddly scientifically literate Beer Commercials. An entertaining and enlightening review of all the science that our favorite movies got wrong, combined with some of the stuff they got right. Incorporates recent films as well as some classics that you may not have known had any science in them at all. ABOUT NEIL DEGRASSE TYSON Neil deGrasse Tyson was born and raised in New York City where he was educated in the public schools clear through his graduation from the Bronx High School of Science. Tyson went on to earn his BA in Physics from Harvard and his PhD in Astrophysics from Columbia. In 2001, Tyson was appointed by President Bush to serve on a twelve-member commission that studied the Future of the U.S. Aerospace Industry. The final report was published in 2002 and contained recommendations (for Congress and for the major agencies of the government) that would promote a thriving future of transportation, space exploration, and national security.

events.title: Edmund Fitzgerald: A Great Lakes Memorial
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: This annual event commemorates the sinking of the freighter Edmund Fitzgerald and the total loss of the 29 crew members aboard on November 10, 1975. It is also a time to reflect on the memory of all lives lost on the Great Lakes. The lighthouse, fog signal building, and visitor center will be open for visitors. Guides will welcome visitors and provide historic site and shipwreck information. Throughout the day, visitors can watch a film about Edmund Fitzgerald in the visitor center, or join a guided tour exploring the history of Fitzgerald’s final voyage. At 4:15 pm, the lighthouse will temporarily close while the names of the crew are read to the tolling of a ship’s bell, with a rendition of the Naval Hymn. Following the ceremony, the beacon will be lit, and the tower will be open again to tour until close at 6 pm. Be sure to bring a flashlight or headlamp as the grounds and trails are unlit. The weather is unpredictable, please dress accordingly. The event will be streamed on Split Rock’s Facebook Page and the Minnesota Historical Society’s YouTube channel. Tickets are offered online and onsite. Tickets only guarantee you admission to the site and program.

events.title: Pruitt Center Virtual Speaker: Shawn Achor – The Power of Belief
events.description: Join us for the Pruitt Center Fall 2026 Virtual Speaker, Shawn Achor! Conventional wisdom holds that success is determined by talent, intelligence or the circumstances we happen to land in. After more than a decade of research at Harvard and work in 51 countries, Shawn Achor found that the greatest predictor of our future success is something else entirely: the set of beliefs we hold about the world around us. Beliefs are not passive. They shape what we notice, how we interpret setbacks, how much energy and persistence we bring to hard problems and whether we see a challenge as fixed or changeable. And because beliefs spread through teams the same way emotions do, a single person’s belief about what is possible can raise—or quietly cap—the ceiling for an entire organization. In his newest book, The Power of Beliefs, Shawn demonstrates that these beliefs are far more malleable than we assume, and that changing them is one of the fastest levers we have for changing performance.

events.title: Urinetown Presented By Zeitgeist Theater Co.
events.description: URINETOWN By Mark Hollmann and Greg Kotis Directed by Robert Lee Musical Direction by Beth Brophy Winner of three Tony Awards, three Outer Critics Circle Awards, two Lucille Lortel Awards and two Obie Awards, Urinetown is a hilarious musical satire of the legal system, capitalism, social irresponsibility, populism, environmental collapse, privatization of natural resources, bureaucracy, municipal politics, and musical theatre itself! Hilariously funny and touchingly honest, Urinetown provides a fresh perspective on one of America’s greatest art forms. In a Gotham-like city, a terrible water shortage, caused by a 20-year drought, has led to a government-enforced ban on private toilets. The citizens must use public amenities, regulated by a single malevolent company that profits by charging admission for one of humanity’s most basic needs. Amid the people, a hero decides that he’s had enough and plans a revolution to lead them all to freedom! Inspired by the works of Bertolt Brecht and Kurt Weill, Urinetown is an irreverently humorous satire in which no one is safe from scrutiny.

events.title: The Oak Ridge Boys
events.description: Friday, November 13, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Pepper Entertainment HERE ABOUT THE OAK RIDGE BOYS For more than 50 years, The Oak Ridge Boys have defined one of the most recognizable sounds in American music, blending four-part harmonies with an energetic stage presence that has earned them Grammy, CMA, ACM, and Dove Awards. With a legacy that stretches from their Gospel roots in the 1940s to their rise as Country‐Pop hitmakers, the group—Duane Allen, Joe Bonsall, William Lee Golden, and Richard Sterban—has delivered classics like Elvira, Bobbie Sue, American Made, and Thank God for Kids. Their music has produced multiple gold and platinum albums, over 30 Top Ten hits, and collaborations with icons ranging from Johnny Cash and Paul Simon to George Jones and Ray Charles. Today’s performing members are Duane Allen, William Lee Golden, Richard Sterban, and Ben James. The Oak Ridge Boys remain one of the most enduring and dynamic touring acts in the world, known for a high‐energy show that celebrates both their rich history and their continued evolution.

events.title: Tea Talks – Adam Sippola – Presence: Gateway to Healing and Awakening
events.description: Presence: Gateway to Healing and Awakening Presence is the conscious devotion to be with the movements of life. Where inner presence is the cultivation of awareness, living stillness, and flow within the body, in relational presence we commit to a moment-by-moment conscious relationship with the forces of creation alive and moving within us, between us, and among us in the shared group field. We will explore the relationship between presence and the healing of trauma – our unintegrated past, and how inner and relational presence practices can support our embodiment (incarnation), as well as our awakening (transcendence). In this interactive discussion and experience, Adam will lead the group in relational presence practices including meditation, interoception, embodiment, attunement, and relational mindfulness, and he may guide an integration process if anyone present feels called to participate. Welcome to Tea Talks, interesting talks by interesting people about topics they are passionate about, in a cozy and informal space.

events.title: Annual Native American Heritage Day
events.description: The St. Louis County Historical Society, under the guidance of the SLCHS American Indian Advisory Committee, is proud to announce its annual Native American Heritage Day from 11 AM to 3 PM on Saturday, November 14, 2026. This year’s event is in partnership with the University of Minnesota-Duluth’s American Indian Learning Resource Center and Indigenous Student Organization and will be held in the Kirby Ballroom at the University of Minnesota-Duluth. The event is free and open to all. Native American Heritage Day gives anyone who is curious the opportunity to see, hear, and taste our regional Ojibwe culture. The theme of this year’s event is Native Creativity. Chat with local Ojibwe artists, view their work, and learn more about how Native identity influences their creativity. There will be opportunities to purchase artwork and make crafts of your own! The Historical Society will also be unveiling the design for our new Lake Superior Ojibwe Gallery, scheduled to open in June 2027. Gary Lundstrom, exhibit designer and fabricator, has constructed a scale model of the new exhibit, which will be on display at the SLCHS table.

events.title: Room for Grief
events.description: A Peer-led gathering on Grief, Gratitude, & Belonging Grief is not a problem to be solved, but an experience to be witnessed. Grief, when shared, becomes a bridge that connects us rather than a burden that isolates us; and offers an opportunity for finding authentic healing. We will speak from personal experience, listen with curiosity, and honor different ways of responding to grief. We will ground ourselves, share what brings us to the space, as well as what we are taking with us as we leave. As our monthly gatherings evolve, participants and community members will be invited to share the particular gifts and skills they have to offer this collective experience of grief. This may include singing, movement, breath work, and other embodied practices. Participants are welcome to bring something to add to the altar that represents their experience of grief. Bio: Paula Williams will hold the space for these peer-led gatherings.

events.title: Songfield
events.description: Songfield is a gathering space for singing rooted in relational presence. We connect through song, embodiment, and relational mindfulness practices, inviting a more conscious music making experience to deepen our aliveness as we play and create in the group field. We learn simple songs together, including folk, traditional, spiritual, chant, and we allow space for organic musical expression. We explore how becoming more present and attuned to our bodies and with one another can enhance our singing with more truthful expression, love, passion, and a fuller spectrum of our humanness. While we practice together, we also focus on the quality of connection between us, drawing closer to what matters as we cultivate and nourish the ground of relationship from which our singing arises. What a Songfield Gathering Includes · Warming up our voices and bodies. · Learning and singing songs together. · Relational Fielding practices supporting attunement, authenticity, connection, and coherence. · More singing! · Guided healing integration when processes arise organically · Group reflections.

events.title: Antique Appraisal
events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society.

events.title: Urinetown Presented By Zeitgeist Theater Co.
events.description: URINETOWN By Mark Hollmann and Greg Kotis Directed by Robert Lee Musical Direction by Beth Brophy Winner of three Tony Awards, three Outer Critics Circle Awards, two Lucille Lortel Awards and two Obie Awards, Urinetown is a hilarious musical satire of the legal system, capitalism, social irresponsibility, populism, environmental collapse, privatization of natural resources, bureaucracy, municipal politics, and musical theatre itself! Hilariously funny and touchingly honest, Urinetown provides a fresh perspective on one of America’s greatest art forms. In a Gotham-like city, a terrible water shortage, caused by a 20-year drought, has led to a government-enforced ban on private toilets. The citizens must use public amenities, regulated by a single malevolent company that profits by charging admission for one of humanity’s most basic needs. Amid the people, a hero decides that he’s had enough and plans a revolution to lead them all to freedom! Inspired by the works of Bertolt Brecht and Kurt Weill, Urinetown is an irreverently humorous satire in which no one is safe from scrutiny.

events.title: Veterans Memorial Hall Annual Remembrance Dinner on 12/03/2026
events.description: Purchase Tickets Online Join us for the 21st annual Veterans Memorial Hall Remembrance Dinner on Thursday, December 3, 2026, in the Great Hall at the St. Louis County Depot. This year’s keynote presentation, “Shipbuilding in the Twin Ports During World War II,” will be presented by Stephen B. Daniel. During World War II, shipyards throughout Duluth and Superior built military and support vessels for the war effort. Stephen Daniel will explore where these ships were built, the types of vessels produced, and the people who worked in the local shipyards, including the important role women played as many men left the region for military service. The evening begins with a social hour at 5:00 p.m., followed by dinner at 6:00 p.m. and the keynote presentation at 7:00 p.m. Dinner will be catered by Valentini’s, and guests may also participate in a silent auction. Tickets are $65 per person. Join us for an evening of remembrance and local history, highlighting the remarkable contribution the Twin Ports made to America’s World War II effort.

events.title: Drooling Pianos
events.description: Thursday, December 17 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm ON SALE NOW Superior native and professional pianist Russ King and stand-up comedian Chris Covert are bringing Drooling Pianos, their adults-only comedy and music show, to DECC Symphony Hall for a special holiday performance Thursday, December 17 at 7 p.m. Drooling Pianos combines live music, stand-up comedy, original and parody songs, improvisation and audience interaction into an unpredictable show built around the very different backgrounds of its two performers. King is an accomplished pianist, songwriter and producer with a career spanning live performance, recording and touring. Covert comes from the world of stand-up comedy and has performed alongside nationally known comedians including Jeff Ross. Put the two together, and things got hilariously inappropriate pretty quickly. King and Covert only met in February 2026, but what began as an experiment combining live music and stand-up comedy quickly gained an audience. Drooling Pianos has already sold out multiple performances, including its debut, and received an enthusiastic response during its Twin Ports appearance at Clyde Iron Works this summer.

events.description: Brace yourself for adventure as we explore the New World’s ties to the old. Whistle & Whiskey brings together the massive hits and nonstop energy of a Flo Rida show with the sound of Mitchell’s country music for a night built to keep fans on their feet. events.title: DSSO Masterworks 5 – In Sacred Light
events.description: A kaleidoscope of perspectives: “My Country ‘Tis of Thee”, filtered through Charles Ives’ shifting lenses. Fragments of a brilliant Schubert symphony left mysteriously unfinished. Tonight’s program represents the American ideal of individual voices converging into one, unified whole. events.description: Presented by Pepper Entertainment Sunday, February 21, 2027 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm ON SALE NOW ABOUT NEEDTOBREATHE NEEDTOBREATHE is known for their distinctive blend of Americana, alt-rock, and spiritual depth—earning five No. 1 albums, over three billion career streams, sold-out tours, and a devoted global following. The South Carolina–bred group—Bear Rinehart, Josh Lovelace, Tyler Burkum, and Randall Harris—enters a new creative chapter with The Long Surrender, their tenth studio album and first release for MCA. Produced by nine-time GRAMMY-winner Dave Cobb, The Long Surrender captures the band at their most vulnerable and instinctive, recorded largely live and driven by Rinehart’s deeply personal songwriting. Led by the early standout “Momma Loves Me” featuring The Red Clay Strays, the album reflects themes of faith, redemption, and renewed clarity—showcasing a band confident enough to strip everything back and let the songs speak for themselves. “This album really clarified that, as an artist, I’ve got to put my convictions in front of anything else,” says Rinehart.

events.description: Sunday, February 28, 2027 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm PRESALE Wednesday, October 28 at 10am until Thursday, October 29 at 10pm Code: DECC ON SALE Friday, October 30 at 10am ABOUT KANSAS With a legendary career spanning five decades, KANSAS has firmly established itself as one of America’s iconic classic rock bands. This “garage band” from Topeka released their debut album in 1974 after being discovered by Wally Gold, who worked for Don Kirshner, and have gone on to sell more than 30 million albums worldwide. Composing a catalogue that includes sixteen studio albums and five live albums, KANSAS has produced eight gold albums, three sextuple-Platinum albums (Leftoverture, Point of Know Return, Best of KANSAS), one platinum live album (Two for the Show), one quadruple-Platinum single ‘Carry On Wayward Son,’ and another triple-Platinum single ‘Dust in the Wind.’ KANSAS appeared on the Billboard charts for over 200 weeks throughout the ‘70’s and ‘80’s and played to sold-out arenas and stadiums throughout North America, Europe and Japan.

events.description: Thursday, April 22, 2027 | DECC Symphony Hall Season Tickets Available Now! Click HERE to learn more. A Beautiful Noise single tickets go on sale November 13. THE UNTOLD TRUE STORY OF A BROOKLYN KID WHO BECAME A CHART-BUSTING, SHOW-STOPPING, AWARD-WINNING AMERICAN ICON Created in collaboration with Neil Diamond himself, A BEAUTIFUL NOISE is the uplifting true story of how a kid from Brooklyn became a chart-busting, show-stopping American rock icon. With 120 million albums sold, a catalogue of classics like “America,” “Forever in Blue Jeans,” and “Sweet Caroline,” an induction into the Songwriters and Rock and Roll Halls of Fame, a Grammy® Lifetime Achievement Award, and sold-out concerts around the world that made him bigger than Elvis, Neil Diamond’s story was made to shine on Broadway-and head out on the road across America. events.title: Pruitt Center Virtual Speaker: Shawn Achor – The Power of Belief
events.venue: Virtual on Zoom: Register at uwsuper.edu/ShawnAchor to receive the Zoom link.
events.description: Join us for the Pruitt Center Fall 2026 Virtual Speaker, Shawn Achor! Conventional wisdom holds that success is determined by talent, intelligence or the circumstances we happen to land in. After more than a decade of research at Harvard and work in 51 countries, Shawn Achor found that the greatest predictor of our future success is something else entirely: the set of beliefs we hold about the world around us. Beliefs are not passive. They shape what we notice, how we interpret setbacks, how much energy and persistence we bring to hard problems and whether we see a challenge as fixed or changeable. And because beliefs spread through teams the same way emotions do, a single person’s belief about what is possible can raise—or quietly cap—the ceiling for an entire organization. In his newest book, The Power of Beliefs, Shawn demonstrates that these beliefs are far more malleable than we assume, and that changing them is one of the fastest levers we have for changing performance.

events.title: The Birch Bark Canoe: A Living Tradition
events.description: Join us at the Ely Folk School to explore the history, design, materials, harvest tools, construction, use and maintenance of the traditional birch bark canoe. events.title: Sew a Sámi-Style Leather Bag or Pouch
events.description: Traditionally used to carry precious commodities like coffee, tobacco and sugar – the Sámi-style leather pouch has been adapted for use by bush craftsmen the world over due to its durable and practical design! Sew and decorate your own pouch while learning about the history of the Sámi in Northern Europe and North America. Highlights of the class include: ● Walk through every step from start to finish to make your personal pouch or bag. ● Work with Swedish reindeer leather, fish leather, wool, woven pewter, glass beads and bone to customize your pouch or bag. ● Gain hands-on experience with Sámi-style sewing and decorative techniques. ● Learn about the culture, techniques, and spiritual connections that make Sámi duodji (traditional handicrafts) so special!

events.title: Community Christmas Caroling
events.description: Get bundled up and join us in the Ely Folk School “Pocket Park” on Christmas Eve Eve for some good old fashioned Christmas caroling! This will be a great opportunity for community members of all ages to gather together in song. No professional singing experience required–if you’ve sang in the car or in the shower then you’re already overqualified! This is simply a way to celebrate the holiday season with your neighbors. Raise your voice to classics like Jingle Bells, Deck the Halls, and Silent Night, before dispersing into the calm darkness of downtown Ely. Lyrics sheets and some percussion instruments will be provided. Hot cocoa provided. See you there!

events.title: Holiday Cookie Swap
events.description: Come fill up your cookie jar with a variety of cookies this winter! Bring your best holiday cookies and join The Ely Folk School for a holiday exchange. Many of us have favorite cookie recipes and stories to accompany them. Please, prepare a couple batches of your favorite or most treasured homemade cookies to bring. We’ll ask everyone to share their recipe and a story about why they made that cookie recipe. Learn about the cookie traditions of your neighbors, take home new recipes, and enjoy a plate full of treats! Please plan to bring along about 2 dozen cookies and a take-home container, and plan to leave with a variety of cookies from friends. Bring along a printed recipe if possible. We will also be joined by the Ely Community Resource Friday Network, who will be baking and participating in the Swap as part of their weekly programming. All ages are welcome–this will be a truly intergenerational event for sharing something we all love: traditions, holidays, and sugar!

events.title: Winter Bonfire
events.description: Our sixth annual Winter Bonfire! All are invited to this free kickoff to winter gathering. We’ll have snacks and refreshments, and some friendly Wintergreen dogsledding dogs who’d love to say hello! Individuals and families are encouraged to join in the potluck fun, or just bundle up and enjoy the cozy winter atmosphere. Additionally interested volunteers can help make sweet apple hand-pies as part of our Makers Morning the Thursday preceding the bonfire on Thursday, December 10th between 9:30am and noon. Thank you to Wintergreen Dogsled Lodge and Piragis Northwoods Company for their support. Please note that due to past weather patterns and predicted temperatures, this year’s bonfire will not be held at Semer’s Park and instead take place in our “pocket park” where there is a warm indoor space to allow everyone in our community to be safe and comfortable!

events.title: Volunteer Hand Pie Assembly
events.description: Join us during our usual Makers Morning for a special volunteer event aimed at getting us prepped for our Winter Bonfire! Volunteers will take pre-made pie dough (created by staff and students the night before at the “Do It Yourself Hand Pies” class) and assembly them into delectable savory hand pies. Ingredients may include zucchini, onion, mushrooms, garlic, and fresh herbs! We need all hands on deck to make enough hand pies for the Winter Bonfire on December 12th, where we celebrate the return of the land to ice and snow, and prepare for a season of communal rest and reset. This fun annual event is a great way to contribute to the community event, and glean some tips and tricks for assembling your own hand pies in the future. All ingredients and equipment will be provided by the Ely Folk School (including aprons) so just show up to help out.

events.title: Thanksgiving Potluck 4 PM
events.description: Join the Ely Folk School on Thanksgiving for a potluck at 4pm! Due to the popularity of this beloved tradition, we will be hosting two different time slots on Thanksgiving to accommodate as much food and people as possible. Help us spread out the day and join us in community at the Ely Folk School. This annual tradition is a great way to celebrate the community-centric day, even if you do not have holiday traditions in Ely yet. Perhaps this will be your new tradition! We hope you’ll enjoy our RENOVATED kitchen space, optimized both for community potlucks (like this one!) and for our Nourishment classes. We would love for you to bring something to share, though it is not required. EFS will ensure there is turkey! Please bring whatever you feel energized about making (or purchasing).

events.title: An Evening of Story, Herbalism, & Wilderness
events.description: An Evening of Story, Herbalism, & Wilderness with Kelly Cramer & Tracy Koivisto: Celebrating Star Roots, a novel inspired by Ely and the healing power of plants. Join local author, artist, and EFS instructor Kelly Cramer for an inspiring evening celebrating the release of her mythic fantasy novel, Star Roots. Hosted at the Ely Folk School, this special event explores the creative heart of the novel and its deep connections to Ely and the natural landscape of Northern Minnesota. All this and more are packed into this special event! Author Presentation & Talk: Discover the inspiration behind Star Roots, its themes, tropes, and characters, and learn how the writing process intersects with a life rooted in local artistry and independent publishing. Immersive Reading: Experience a special reading featuring an audio recording of the book’s narrator paired with an ambient forest projection. Art & Visual Displays: View custom woodburned art pieces created specifically to accompany the story, displayed alongside Kelly’s book, and a short-story that started it all.

events.title: Old Time Strings Jam Session
events.description: Come on down for an old time strings music jam session at the Ely Folk School! Bring a fiddle, banjo, guitar, mandolin, dulcimer, or bass to EFS! Play along, or just sit back and listen. Everyone, no matter your skill or comfort level, is welcome to play along, listen, or even dance. These jam sessions have an emphasis on string instruments. It is a jam session, so sheet music is not provided, rather chords are called out. Joe Smith, Ely resident and long time jam member, will be helping to lead the string session and will provide a list of songs that will likely be covered during the jam (coming soon.) Rgistration not required, and the jam is open to all. Folks are welcome to play, or just come and listen.

events.title: Community Sing
events.description: Join us on the first Tuesday of every month for community singing. Simply show up (registration is not required) and join the circle of voices. Music will be taught the night of; all voices are welcome to gather and be led in song. There are no auditions or music to read, no performances, and little to no accompanying instrumentation. Community Sing is an entirely oral tradition for people of all ages! Unlike a choir, Community Sing is not divided by traditional voice parts or vocal range. Some songs are sung all together, as call-and-response, in a round, or in taught parts. Community Sing is also non-denominational.

events.title: Zaverl’s Meat Raffle
events.description: Come on out to support the Ely Folk School at our annual Meat Raffle hosted at Zaverl’s Bar. This casual and fun night is an easy way to support the Ely Folk School’s mission of building community via intergenerational learning experiences. Trays of meat from Zup’s will be raffled off throughout the evening for $2/ticket. No registration needed! Win yourself a turkey, ham, pork chops, or a number of different frozen treats plus a variety of wines to pair.

events.title: Ely Area Writer’s Group
events.description: The mission of the Ely Area Writers Group (formerly Writers Read) is to encourage writers to write. Writers tend to hide their work. For most, the only thing worse than rejection is having something printed that isn’t perfect, so we give gentle suggestions for edits and cheer all the good bits. When someone joins our group, we add their email to our list. Before our monthly meetings, anyone can submit something they’ve written to the group via email. Any genre is welcome. The author may be specific about what response they want (does this essay flow, or is this character believable, or which images stick with you?) or they can let the others respond on any aspect that strikes them. Some members submit work every month, others may share something only a few times a year. Registration is not required; simply show up!

The author may be specific about what response they want (does this essay flow, or is this character believable, or which images stick with you?) or they can let the others respond on any aspect that strikes them. Some members submit work every month, others may share something only a few times a year. Registration is not required; simply show up!

events.title: Sashiko – Japanese Embroidery (3 Session Class)
events.description: Price:Tuition: $90, Materials: $13 Step into the world of Sashiko needlework with artist and educator Akiko Ostlund. This versatile traditional Japanese stitching and embroidery technique was primarily used to mend, reinforce, and embellish garments. In this class, you will learn the history of Sashiko, how to select and handle materials, try its basic running stitches, learn some traditional patterns and their meanings. We will also practice visible mending using this practical yet decorative stitching technique that embodies sustainability, community, and simplicity. All materials provided. This hands-on workshop welcomes artists of all levels.

events.title: Empowering Celebration of Creativity
events.description: Gather for our community Sew-She-O-Lite craft and sewing event. Discover the transformative power of friendship and art, as research reveals that regular connections with like-minded individuals foster happiness, well-being, and serenity. Our sewing group embodies this spirit, offering a nurturing environment where imagination flourishes, and kindred spirits come together to inspire and uplift each other. In the pursuit of cultivating vibrant community lives, the Embarrass Town Board warmly invites you to our monthly Sew/craft-in days, that originally, began in May 2023. Bring your chosen craft and supplies, and join our vibrant community! Let’s share snacks, beverages, and lunch together, potluck-style, and infuse our gathering with laughter and joy. For inquiries, kindly reach out to Lex McDonald or Shireen Lee.

events.title: Caregiver Support Group
events.address: Northwoods Partners 760 Miners Dr., Suite 500 Ely, MN 55731
events.description: Caregiving is a tough and isolating experience. Caregiver support groups provide an opportunity to connect with others that are in similar situations. Support group members validate each other’s experiences. These groups are a great place to ask for advice, find out about useful resources, and safely vent your frustrations. Nobody will judge you, because everyone there is going through many of the same struggles. It’s a safe place to share your feelings and get the support you need. You are not alone!

All are welcome, no matter skill level or (reasonable) project type. A space to share projects and work in a community setting are important! Drop in whenever as you like, for as long as you like. events.title: SAIL- Stay Active and Independent for life
events.description: Stay Active and Independent for Life! The SAIL exercise class is a strength, balance, and fitness program for community dwelling older adults that meets two to three times per work for one hour. Performing exercises that improve strength, balance, and fitness is the single most important activity adults can do to stay active and reduce their chances of falling. The entire curriculum of activities in the SAIL program can help improve strength and balance, if done regularly.

events.title: Community Sing
events.description: Join us on the first Tuesday of every month for community singing. Simply show up (registration is not required) and join the circle of voices. Music will be taught the night of; all voices are welcome to gather and be led in song. There are no auditions or music to read, no performances, and little to no accompanying instrumentation. Community Sing is an entirely oral tradition for people of all ages! Unlike a choir, Community Sing is not divided by traditional voice parts or vocal range. Some songs are sung all together, as call-and-response, in a round, or in taught parts. Community Sing is also non-denominational. This recurring monthly event has no cover charge, though donations are always appreciated. Thank you Chickadee-Dee-Dee for leading us in song!

events.title: Monthly Luncheon – Behind the Magic at The Reif: A Special Chamber Luncheon On-Site!
events.description: Ever wonder what happens behind the curtain before the lights come up and the show begins? Join us at The Reif for a special Chamber luncheon that takes you beyond the audience seats and into the world of live theatre! Enjoy lunch and networking, experience a special live performance featuring Reif Theater Arts’ production of Disney’s Aladdin JR., and get a behind-the-scenes look at the props, costumes, and creative details that help bring a production to life. Whether you love the arts, enjoy seeing local talent in action, or are simply curious about what goes into putting on a show, this is a chance to experience The Reif in a whole new way. Come for lunch, stay for the magic! Location The Reif 720 NW Conifer Dr. Grand Rapids, MN 55744 Schedule 11:45 a.m. – Arrival and networking 11:45 a.m.–12:15 p.m. – Lunch in the lobby 12:15–12:20 p.m. – Move into the theater 12:20–12:40 p.m. – Aladdin JR. live performance highlights 12:40–1:00 p.m. – Behind the Magic: a backstage peek at props, costumes, and the details that bring a show to life 1:00 p.m.

events.title: Chamber Board Member Interest
events.description: There’s a Seat at the Table. Could It Be Yours? LOOKING FOR LEADERS: Who care about business. Who care about our community. Who want to help shape what comes next. The Grand Rapids Area Chamber of Commerce is accepting applications for upcoming seats on its Board of Directors. Serving on the Chamber Board is an opportunity to bring your perspective to the table, help guide the priorities and direction of the organization, and be part of conversations that impact businesses throughout our area. Why Serve? As a Chamber Board member, you will have the opportunity to: • Help shape Chamber priorities, programs, and advocacy efforts. • Represent the perspectives and needs of our business community. • Build relationships with business and community leaders. • Contribute your experience, ideas, and perspective to the Chamber’s future. • Help strengthen the business environment in the Grand Rapids area. Who Are We Looking For? We are looking for engaged, thoughtful leaders who care about business and our community and are willing to actively participate in the work of the Chamber.

events.title: Taking Care of Business
events.description: Get your business in front of Chamber members and the public at Taking Care of Business, our fun and festive December networking and marketing event! This event is designed to give Chamber members a unique opportunity to showcase their business, make connections, and engage with attendees in a relaxed, interactive setting. Vendor space is limited to 55 businesses, so early registration is encouraged. SANTA SERFLING RETURNS THIS YEAR! Thank you to Rapids Riders ATV Club! Vendor participation is $175 and includes: 6-foot table, chairs, and table covering Opportunity to promote your business to Chamber members and the public Free appetizers for attendees, sponsored by Paul Bunyan Communications Participation in our vendor game and event activities To help make the event interactive, participating businesses are asked to bring a simple game or activity for their booth, along with a door prize. Vendor setup begins at 2:30 PM Only 55 vendor spaces are available. To reserve your vendor space: TAKING CARE OF BUSINESS (*To register, you must use an email address/contact associated to your GrowthZone Member account.)

events.title: Monthly Luncheon – IEDC: Connecting Business, Community & Opportunity – Building a Stronger Itasca County
events.description: There’s a lot happening across Itasca County, and Itasca Economic Development Corporation (IEDC) is positioning itself to help businesses and communities make the most of the opportunities ahead. Join us for a look at the organization’s renewed direction, emerging economic opportunities, and the partnerships helping shape our region’s future. From strengthening existing businesses and supporting entrepreneurs to connecting local companies with resources, investment, and new opportunities for growth, IEDC will share what the organization is working on, what’s ahead for 2027, and how we can work together to build a stronger regional economy. And since it’s December, Christmas sweaters are encouraged (but completely optional)!

events.title: TRUEGRASS WITH FLUTES & LOW
events.description: TrueGrass brings old-style bluegrass to The Backstage, covering material by classic bluegrass bands while also adapting modern material and originals to the bluegrass tradition. The group features guitar, clawhammer banjo, banjo, dobro, bass, fiddle, and vocals.

events.title: Mt Ashwabay Ski & Snowboard Swap
events.venue: Mt. Ashwabay Ski and Recreation Area
events.address: Mt. Ashwabay Ski and Recreation Area
events.description: Affordable winter fun starts right here at Mt. Ashwabay. Winter adventures shouldn't come with a hefty price tag! Whether you're outfitting growing kids, trying a new winter sport, or just looking for a great deal, the Mt. Ashwabay Ski + Snowboard Swap is the place to start. Shop gently used downhill skis, snowboards, Nordic gear, boots, winter clothing, and more—all while supporting the hill we love. And here's the best part: 20% of every sale goes directly to the Ashwabay Alliance , helping support outdoor programs, hill improvements, and scholarships that make winter recreation more accessible to our community. Because when we shop local, share what we have, and support one another, we keep more people playing outside! SKI + SNOWBOARD SWAP Mt. Ashwabay | Bayfield, WI NOV 7, 2026 10AM-2PM ITEM DROP-OFF: NOV 4TH - 6TH 10AM-5PM ITEM PICK UP: NOV. 9TH - 11TH 10AM-5PM Great gear. Fresh adventures. A stronger community.

events.title: Claire & Ellen's Winter Book Club
events.description: Join us for a deeper dive into books with some great company with Claire Duquette & Ellen Akins. Second Wednesdays Nov-April 6-7pm. Nov 11 Yesteryear, Caro Claire Burke Dec 9 Mrs. Caliban, Rachel Ingalls Jan 13 The Tiger’s Wife, Tea Obreht Feb 10 Small things Like These, Claire Keegan March 10 Life After Life, Kate Atkinson April 14 Sea of Tranquility, Emily St. John Mandel Everyone Welcome. You do not need to “join.” Come whenever it works or the book strikes your fancy. The Book Bar will be open serving wine, cider, beer & NA drinks + sandwiches and pizzas. Claire Duquette is the former editor of the Ashland Daily Press and continues to write about books and the arts. She is the assistant manager at Honest Dog Books where you’ll find her behind the counter Saturdays selecting books for the store’s SurpriseMe! Subscription. Ellen Akins is the author of the novels Home Movie (1988), Little Woman (1990), Public Life (1993), and Hometown Brew (1998), and the short story collection World Like a Knife (1991). She writes book reviews for national publications like the Washington Post and Star Tribune and loves talking books. Recurring monthly on the 2nd Wednesday.

events.title: Crafting Traditional Soap
events.description: Friday November 13th 2026, 5:30pm - 7pm Step into the timeless craft of soap making with artisan soap maker Lindsay Larson. In this class, you’ll be guided through the complete process of creating handcrafted soap using reclaimed animal fat; a sustainable, traditional ingredient once used in every homestead kitchen. Together, we’ll explore the alchemy of transforming rendered fat, lye, and botanicals into a cleansing, nourishing bar of soap. You’ll learn about safety practices, temperature control, ingredient selection, and mold preparation, along with tips on sourcing high-quality materials and natural additives. This is a guided learning experience, perfect for anyone curious about the old ways of soap making and eager to bring this lost art back into their own home practice. Consider bringing: A notebook and writing utensil You Receive: Step by step notes on soap making, one bar of the soap made in class.

What You’ll Experience Shop local handmade apparel, jewelry, decor and more while supporting Madeline Island community artists Pick up holiday gifts for friends, family and loved ones Enjoy refreshments served during the event About the Location: Bella and Leo Capser opened the Madeline Island Museum in 1958. events.title: Dickens of a Christmas Dinner Theater * A Dickensian Dream: An Evening of A Christmas Carol & Victorian Feast
events.description: The holiday tradition continues! As the story of Scrooge, Marley, and the Ghosts of Christmas Past unfolds, you will enjoy a sumptuous four-course Victorian-style meal . Each course is expertly paired with select White Winter meads, ciders, and spirits, chosen by Meadmaker Jon himself. Indulge in the flavors of a Dickensian Christmas with our complete menu: Don’t miss this perfect blend of literature, fine dining, and holiday cheer! We sell out early every year so buy soon to guarantee your place at the table!

events.title: Mary Mack Comedy
events.description: Let's slide in to fall with some good humor! This PG13 stand-up comedy show features material Mary has generated the last couple years for her 9th album recording in December 2026. And we hear through the grapevine, she may be bringing a secret musical guest. Yahoooo! Tickets: $20 in Advance, $25 at the door. Free for Union members Doors Open: 6pm Show Starts: 7pm More about the comedian: Comedian Mary Mack has been featured on Conan, The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon, Comedy Central, Dry Bar Comedy, and more. A hybrid of Minnesota and Wisconsin, with a severe cheese dependency, Mack is a favorite on radio shows and podcasts around the country including, Marc Maron's WTF Podcast, The Bob and Tom Show, The Grand Ole Opry and SiriusXM comedy channels. Currently, she stars as Jesse in the cult-favorite Hulu cartoon Solar Opposites, and she voices several characters on Disney +’s Kiff. She is a proud SAG-AFTRA union member. More info at MaryMackComedy.com.

events.title: City Council Pre-Agenda Meeting
events.description: The 5:00 p.m. pre-agenda meeting is a work session between the City Council and City staff to review the upcoming City Council meeting agenda, future meeting agendas, and is a time for the City Council and City staff to have discussions about the agenda items and asking and answering questions. The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Although pre-agenda meetings are open to the public, it is not a time for public comment, as the public can listen to the conversation and ask questions or provide input at the upcoming City Council meeting. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6.

events.title: City Council Meeting
events.description: In-Person Access The 6:00 p.m. City Council Meetings are open to the public and held in council chambers at the Proctor Area Community Center (PACC) 100 Pionk Drive Proctor, MN. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6. Remote Access The 6:00 p.m. City Council Meeting is available remotely via YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@trac7298/streams. Public comments may also be submitted in advance of the meeting to cityhall@proctormn.gov up to 3:00 p.m. the day of the meeting with the e-mail title “City Council Meeting.”

events.title: Retail Employee Day
events.description: Today the City of Proctor proudly recognizes the hardworking team at Mountain Spirits Municipal Liquor Store in honor of Retail Employees’ Day. Retail Employees’ Day celebrates the dedicated people who keep stores running and ensure customers have a positive shopping experience. From helping customers find the perfect bottle, stocking shelves, managing inventory, and keeping the store welcoming and organized, retail employees play an important role in connecting products with the people who enjoy them. At Mountain Spirits, our team works year-round to provide friendly service, maintain a well-stocked store, and support this City or Proctor’s municipal enterprises. Their efforts help make shopping easy, enjoyable, and welcoming for everyone who walks through the door. Please join us in thanking the Mountain Spirits staff for their hard work, professionalism, and commitment to serving the Proctor community. Your dedication does not go unnoticed!

events.title: Public Health and Human Services Board Meeting
events.description: PUBLIC HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES BOARD The Human Services Board includes the 5 county commissioners and the chairs of the PHHS Advisory Committee and Local Mental Health Advisory Committee. The board has authority to administer all public health and human services programs. Some of the Board’s specific functions are: set policy; appropriate funds and approve expenditures, monitor agency progress toward outcomes; assure adequate staffing for program delivery and advocate for changes to meet the needs of the local community.

events.title: Holiday High Tea
events.description: ✨ Event Highlights: • Classic English Tea Service: Assorted sandwiches, sweets, scones and tea • Cash Bar: Specialty holiday-themed cocktails • Live Entertainment: A narrated synopsis of The Nutcracker by Minnesota Ballet dancers • Craft Corner: Decorate your own gingerbread cookie • Photo Station: Pose with ballerinas and Nutcracker characters in a turn-of-the-century-inspired setting • Discounted Minnesota Ballet merchandise & tickets available onsite 🎄 Special Offer for Families Receive $5 off children’s tickets when you purchase two or more using promo code TEA4THREE at checkout! 💎VIP Upgrades Available Treat yourself or someone special to the VIP experience, featuring: Priority seating at a private table A complimentary cocktail or mocktail A nutcracker-themed souvenir/toy Whether you’re continuing a family tradition or creating a new one, the Holiday High Tea with the Minnesota Ballet is a heartwarming way to celebrate the season.

events.title: The Nutcracker: A Duluth Tale
events.description: The holiday tradition that leaves every audience spellbound — this season featuring Tchaikovsky’s beloved score performed live by the Duluth Superior Symphony Orchestra. Performance at 7:00 pm on December 11, and 3:00 pm on December 12-13, 2026, at DECC’s Symphony Hall. Tickets available through Ticketmaster, or save more than $20/ticket in fees by calling the Minnesota Ballet Box Office (218-733-7570) to reserve your seats.

events.title: Coppelia
events.description: One of the most beloved comic ballets of the 19th century, Coppélia tells the story of the clever and spirited Swanilda, who outwits an eccentric toymaker and wins back her wayward fiancé — all with irresistible charm and Léo Delibes’ glorious score. Pure joy from start to finish, and a perfect introduction to ballet for the whole family. Performance at 7:00 pm on March 12 and 3:00 pm on March 13-14, 2027, at UMD’s Marshall Performing Arts Center.

events.title: The Mighty Casey
events.description: A Dance Doubleheader not to be missed — The Mighty Casey brings America’s most famous baseball poem to vivid life through dance, paired with original works by Minnesota Ballet’s own faculty and company dancers. An evening that swings for the fences. Performance at 7:00 pm on April 23 and 3:00 pm on April 24-25, 2027 at The Depot Theater.

events.title: Beginning Clay with Matt Larson
events.description: Location details The Duluth Art Institute’s Lincoln Park Building (2229 W 2nd Street) houses a fully equipped ceramics studio accommodating beginning to advanced potters and ceramic artists. The studio provides throwing wheels, hand-building and wedging tables, a slab roller, spray booth, glaze room, and related hand tools. The studio also boasts four electric kilns and one large gas kiln. Learn more about the ceramic studio What does this class pricing support? As a local nonprofit, the Duluth Art Institute is committed to compensating our instructors, keeping class sizes small for personalized learning, providing quality tools and materials, and supporting our continued operation. Thank you for taking part in our creative community! Questions?

events.title: Jazz at the Lake Superior Railroad Museum
events.description: JAZZ at the Depot Returns! Great jazz. Historic trains. Good food and drinks. What better way to spend a winter Saturday? One of Duluth’s favorite winter traditions is back! JAZZ at the Depot, sponsored by Krenzen, brings the sounds of live jazz to the historic Lake Superior Railroad Museum inside the St. Louis County Depot in downtown Duluth. Every Saturday afternoon throughout the winter season, continuing through April, enjoy live music from the former Club Saratoga Jazz Quartet, performing trackside among the museum’s historic locomotives and railcars. From the swinging big-band sounds of Duke Ellington, Count Basie and Glenn Miller to the timeless tunes of Benny Goodman, Thelonious Monk and other jazz greats, there’s something for longtime jazz fans and casual listeners alike. Led by Randy Lee, the quartet delivers an afternoon of classic favorites, modern jazz and entertaining musical commentary. Make an afternoon of it! Admission is just $7 per person, including the cash bar. Warm up with complimentary coffee and hot cocoa, or grab something tasty from the concession stand, featuring gourmet hot dogs, snacks and freshly popped popcorn.
