events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free!

events.title: Intrigue Chocolate Tasting Class
events.description: Intrigue Chocolate Tasting Class 📅 Date: November 12 ⏰ Time: 5:00-7:30pm 💵 Price: $48 (+ $2 processing fee) 🎟️ Register online: ! Indulge your sweet tooth with a 1-hour tasting and education session with local chocolate makers! During this class, you’ll delve into the science of flavor, gain insight into the chocolate-making process, and taste your way through various chocolate products (cacao tea, roasted cacao beans, and six different chocolate bars) with Aaron Barthel and Karl Mueller, co-owners of Intrigue Chocolate in downtown Chisholm, MN. 🍫☕🤤 About Aaron: Raised in Minnesota, Aaron has worn many hats throughout his life—he’s been a farmer, a botanist, a brewer, a baker, a chef, and a chocolate maker. He’s passionate about small-batch craft chocolate, and he loves experimenting with fruits, herbs, and spices. About Karl: Karl has an entrepreneurial spirit dedicated to taking on what he describes as the ultimate career challenge—building a sustainable and ethical business in the notoriously difficult industry of craft chocolate. He’s also interested in history, culture, and generally making the world a better place.

events.title: Call For Indigenous Artists
events.description: Call for Artists: Our Helpers, a Woodland Anishinaabe/Dakota Art Exhibition 🗓️ Apply now through Friday, November 13, 2026, 11:59pm 👥 Open to all Dakota, Ojibwe, and Ho-Chunk tribal citizens and descendants 👀 Accepting any visual art medium that can be physically displayed ❓ Questions? Accommodation needs? Email art.moira@gmail.com 🖋️ Application: View, fill out, and submit here Calling all Dakota, Ojibwe, and Ho-Chunk artists! MDC is excited to host Our Helpers, a Woodland Anishinaabe/Dakota Art Exhibition in partnership with local Indigenous artists Moira Villiard, Alexis Martinez, and Avery Makes Room For Them. Themed Our Helpers, the exhibit is an invitation to remember that we are never separate from the world around us. It honors the relationship between Indigenous peoples and the living world: animals, plants, water, sky, stars, and spirit. Artists and viewers alike are asked to consider not only who helps us humans, but also how we humans can become better helpers within the ecosystem of this evolving world in which we are all related and interconnected. Interested? Apply online! Applications are open now and close on November 13 at 11:59pm.

events.title: Family Discovery Day: Maamawai Giwii-Kikendamin (Together We Learn)
events.description: 📅 Saturday, November 14 ⏰ 10am–4pm 💸 FREE FOR ALL Join us and our friends from Bois Forte Heritage Center & Cultural Museum for Family Discovery Day: Maamawai Giwii-Kikendamin (Together We Learn) as we celebrate Native American Heritage Month through art, culture, food, music, and community. This FREE, family-friendly event is an opportunity to learn together through stories, shared experiences, and cultural traditions while supporting Indigenous artists, educators, and community members. Throughout the day, guests can participate in hands-on printmaking, enjoy an Ojibwe-inspired meal, and experience a vibrant cultural showcase featuring drumming, singing, and dancing. 🥁🎶 Join Fire in the Village, a collective of artists and cultural organizers, for a printmaking pop-up! Participants are invited to make and take a fabric patch featuring images of Aandeg (Crow), the Fire in the Village emblem, and other artwork created by Anishinaabe artist and director Annie Humphrey (Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe).

events.title: Soldiers of the American Revolution
events.description: 📅 Date: Thursday, November 19 ⏰ Time: 1:00-3:00pm 📍 Place: MDC’s Taconite Square 📚 Host: Chisholm Public Library/Arrowhead Library System 💸 Cost: FREE! Come learn about United States history with a Minnesota-based living history educator! The Arrowhead Library System is pleased to present free history events at participating ALS libraries from October 14 to November 20, 2026. This interactive event, presented by Arn Kind of Historical Experiences, is titled: Soldiers of the American Revolution. On this 250th Anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, join Arn Kind for an event all about the American Revolution. This in-depth presentation puts audience members into the life of a revolutionary soldier with historical artifacts, uniforms, and hands-on experiences. Audiences will enjoy learning about the causes of the revolution and how it led to the birth of the United States of America. This two-hour program is suited for ages 10 and up. This program, sponsored by Arrowhead Library System and hosted by Chisholm Public Library, was funded in part or in whole with money from Minnesota’s Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund (ACHF).

events.title: Trivia
events.description: Clock in. Your brain shift starts now. Trivia is every Thursday night. There are eight rounds, including general knowledge, music, photos, and a few that make you question how you ever knew anything in the first place. Teams can be up to six people. There are prizes for the winners!

events.title: Customer Appreciation Week
events.description: We can’t say this enough: thank you for showing up for us. Whether you’re in every week, make us part of your weekend, bring your friends, or just stop by once in a while, we appreciate every bit of it. We wouldn’t be here without you. There’s a different deal every day from 11 AM–7 PM. Monday: Free Cone Day Get a free small creemee, no purchase necessary. Tuesday: $6 Flights Wednesday: Cider and a Slice A cider and a Wrecktangle Pizza slice for $6. Thursday: Spin the Wheel Spin the prize wheel for a guaranteed win! Friday: Bring a Friend Bring a friend and get buy one, get one on drinks.

events.title: Taylor Swift Singo
events.description: If you know every word to All Too Well (10 Minute Version), this one’s for you. We’re playing Taylor Swift Singo, so get ready for a little music bingo featuring songs from every era. Free to play, prizes up for grabs, and all your favorite songs on the playlist. Grab your Swiftie friends, and we’ll see you there!

events.title: Mandala Rock Painting Class
events.description: Join Ingrid for a relaxing Mandala Rock Painting class. Guests can bring their own rocks or choose from Ingrid’s collection of hand-picked rocks. Painting materials and tools will be provided, along with painted mandala rocks for inspiration. Participants are welcome to create a mandala design or paint their own unique artwork. No experience is necessary, and Ingrid will be available to offer guidance, techniques, and encouragement throughout the class. Registration is $20 per person for the two-and-a-half-hour class. Payment will be collected at the event, with various payment options available. Walk-ins are welcome while supplies last and space is available.

events.title: Adam Sandler Trivia
events.description: Think you know everything about Adam Sandler? Prove it. We’re talking Billy Madison, Happy Gilmore, The Waterboy, Big Daddy, his comedy bits, his life, all of it. If you can quote your favorite Sandler movie by heart, or have ever wondered how many movies one guy can possibly make, this is your night. Teams of up to 6, free to play, prizes for the winners. We also highly encourage your best Adam Sandler fit: oversized basketball shorts, baggy tees, backwards hats, whatever he’d wear on a casual Tuesday. The baggier, the better. You can do it!

events.title: Pitch Your Friend
events.description: Think your friend’s a catch? This is your chance to make your case. Pitch your friend in a 5-minute presentation to a live crowd. Tell us who they are, why someone should date them, and make your best case. Then let the crowd decide who gave the best pitch. The winner gets a prize, and your friend might leave with a date (or a pretty good story). Whether you’re up there pitching your friend, looking to meet someone, or just here for the entertainment, come see what happens. Want to sign up to pitch? Fill out this form.

events.title: And A Court Of Thorns And Roses Trivia
events.description: The courts of Prythian are calling, and it’s time to see who really knows their ACOTAR lore. From the High Lords and the history of each court to epic plot twists and all the details tucked between the pages, we’re putting your knowledge to the test. Grab your Inner Circle for six rounds of trivia! Themed prizes are up for grabs for the winning team, and fae-inspired outfits are encouraged. May the best court win!

events.title: Drag Night
events.description: Catch a drag show by Zenith City Horror on the last Friday of every month! Each show has a new theme, so there’s always something different to look forward to.

events.title: Holiday Gift Market
events.description: Get a little something for your best bud. They deserve it. Shop local vendors, find some one-of-a-kind gifts, and stay warm inside with a hot mulled cider. Featured Vendors: Art by Court Laine Wild Kidd Design Root Cellar Preserves Green Revival Vintage Beautifully Distracted Warm Earth Ceramics Roots and Rises Mama’s Midnight Bakery The Holiday Market is free to attend and open to all ages.

events.title: Guided Watercolor Class
events.description: Join Jordan Larson at Wild State to paint your very own Minnesota loon! No watercolor experience needed. Jordan will walk you through it step by step, from mixing colors to adding the little details that bring your loon to life. You’ll leave with your own 8×10 watercolor painting to take home. Come hang out, get a little creative, and enjoy an afternoon at the taproom.

events.title: Wild Santa 5k & Reindeer Run
events.description: Wild Santa 5K on Saturday, December 12, is a fun run winding through the Lincoln Park Craft District of Duluth, MN. Registration includes a 5-piece Santa suit and a free cider, plus the whole crew can stick around for the all-ages after-party at Wild State Cider. Kids 8 and under can join the Reindeer Run! Reindeer Run registration includes a pair of antlers and entry into the Reindeer Run, a 1/4-mile fun run. Here’s what you can expect: Hundreds of Santas running around the neighborhood A sample of Bent Paddle Brewing Co.’s Christmas Cookie Ale Free cider before or after the race An all-ages after-party & more to be announced! This event is open to all ages. Find more details at wildsantarun.com.

events.title: Art on Tap With Eric Klepinger
events.description: Join us for another fun and creative evening of Art on Tap at Castle Danger Brewery! Each class is led by professional artist and Voyageur Artists member Eric Klepinger. Every session features a new theme and painting style — perfect for both beginners and experienced artists looking to relax, create, and enjoy a cold beer while they paint. For this class, we will be creating 5 x 7 art cards on 140 pound deckle edged watercolor paper using acrylics. This thick paper is wonderful for working with both heavily or watery applied acrylics. Depending on how many attend, each artist should have up to 4 cards to paint on, and each card comes with an envelope. This is a great activity if you wish to give something special to someone that is better than a store-bought card, and the holidays are right around the corner, too! Art cards make great gifts as the recipient can then frame the card as a bit of art. Class is $15 for Voyageur Members, $20 for non-members and $10 for Castle Danger Staff. Class is limited to 16 people, no experience necessary and all the materials will be supplied. Please click on the ‘Tickets’ link to sign-up and arrive by 5:15 pm to secure your place.

events.title: The Rainy Rose Food Trailer (Pop Up)
events.description: Named after their daughters’ middle names, The Rainy Rose is a family-run food trailer owned by Mike and Amy Wahlman. This local favorite brings bold, Mexican-inspired comfort food to the North Shore — crafted with heart, heritage, and serious flavor. From crispy chimichangas and birria tacos to loaded nachos and their fan-favorite Cuban sandwich, the menu at The Rainy Rose offers something for everyone, including delicious jackfruit options for plant-based eaters. Every dish is made from scratch and rooted in Mike’s 20+ years of culinary experience and passion. So what are you waiting for? Grab a bite today!

events.title: Baptism River Barbecue Co. (Pop Up)
events.description: Get ready for some seriously good Northwoods barbecue! Baptism River Barbecue Co. serves its signature smoked meats and scratch-made sides crafted with locally sourced produce, responsibly raised animals, and hardwoods grown along Lake Superior’s North Shore. Founded by husband-and-wife team Dan and Kaylee Cahill Mathews, Baptism River Barbecue Co. brings a warm, community-focused vibe and unforgettable flavors to every visit. Whether you’re craving melt-in-your-mouth brisket, perfectly smoked pulled pork, or hearty homemade sides, their menu delivers comfort, craft, and true North Shore character. Come hungry, grab a pint, and enjoy some of the best barbecue around—right here on the harbor. Follow them: Website: baptismriverbbq.com Instagram: @baptismriver_barbecueco Facebook: Baptism River Barbecue Co.

Baptism River Barbecue Co. serves its signature smoked meats and scratch-made sides crafted with locally sourced produce, responsibly raised animals, and hardwoods grown along Lake Superior’s North Shore. Founded by husband-and-wife team Dan and Kaylee Cahill Mathews, Baptism River Barbecue Co. brings a warm, community-focused vibe and unforgettable flavors to every visit. Whether you’re craving melt-in-your-mouth brisket, perfectly smoked pulled pork, or hearty homemade sides, their menu delivers comfort, craft, and true North Shore character. Come hungry, grab a pint, and enjoy some of the best barbecue around—right here on the harbor. Follow them: Website: baptismriverbbq.com Instagram: @baptismriver_barbecueco Facebook: Baptism River Barbecue Co.

events.title: Trivia Night with TriviaMafia
events.description: Monthly Trivia Night with Trivia Mafia Put your knowledge to the test at Castle Danger Brewery’s Monthly Trivia Night, happening every first Tuesday of the month at 6pm. Gather your friends, grab a pint, and get ready for a fun evening of friendly competition. It’s free to play, and the top three teams will walk away with prizes. Trivia Mafia keeps the questions fresh, challenging, and entertaining—so whether you’re a seasoned trivia buff or just in it for the laughs, there’s something for everyone.

events.title: Meat Raffle
events.description: Meat Raffle at Castle Danger Brewery Get ready for a true Minnesota classic. Join us in the taproom for an evening of cold beer, friendly competition, and community fun at our Meat Raffle, hosted by Two Harbors Moose Lodge 1463, featuring premium cuts from Zup’s Meat Market. Grab your tickets, gather your crew, and take your shot at winning some top-notch meats from Zup’s —all while supporting a great cause. All proceeds benefit the Moose Lodge and the local organizations they serve right here in the Two Harbors community.

events.title: Books and Brews
events.description: Join the Two Harbors Public Library & Castle Danger Brewery every 3rd Tuesday of the month for Books & Brews! From 6-8pm, bring the book you are currently reading and chat with fellow book lovers. No specific genre, no specific title. Anything you are reading! Every book lover who brings their book to chat about will receive $1 off your first beer!

events.title: Brother Ali with DJ Abilities
events.description: Brother Ali is a respected Hip Hop artist, speaker, and community leader. His two-decade resume includes ten critically-acclaimed albums, mentorships with iconic Hip Hop legends Chuck D and Rakim, and performances on late night shows with Jimmy Fallon and Conan O’Brien.His provocative and uplifting brand of Hip Hop has earned him coveted press features like Rolling Stone’s 40th anniversary edition and Source Magazine’s “Hip Hop Quotables”, while his outspoken social justice message has landed him on government watch lists. He’s also lectured at universities from Princeton to Stanford and delivered the keynote address at the Nobel Peace Prize Forum.When he’s not rocking the mic at Coachella or being arrested for civil disobedience in support of marginalized communities, Brother Ali travels the world learning and teaching Islamic Spirituality under some of today’s most renowned teachers. In addition to leading worship services and classes, he co-founded The Gemali Project, an organization that helps Muslim converts and spiritual seekers access the beauty of the Islamic tradition.

events.title: TrueGrass with Flutes & Low
events.description: TrueGrass!® with opening actFlutes & LowTrueGrass! brings tight harmonies, lively picking, and a love of classic bluegrass to the stage, blending traditional favorites with modern material and originals. The band features Tom Draughon on guitar, clawhammer banjo, and lead vocals; Jed Malischke on banjo and dobro; Bruce Qualey on bass; and Carol McDowall on fiddle—and they all sing!Opening the evening is Flutes & Low, the folk duo of Ben Pichler and Cambria Haen. Since meeting in Duluth, they’ve crafted a sound inspired by the Midwest’s landscapes, pairing two voices with simple arrangements and memorable melodies.

Parking:Attendees can park at the base of the mountain at the Grand Avenue Chalet parking lot: 8551 Grand Avenue, Duluth, MN 55808 Come enjoy the fall colors, grab your pass, and spend a fall afternoon on the mountain. events.title: Teacher Training Workshop – Spring Weekend
events.description: Spring Weekend Workshop Join us for our Teacher Training Institute’s (almost) Spring workshop! Learn from Wolf Ridge Naturalists to co-teach in this transitional season of weather (snow, rain), develop your naturalist skills and learn tips and tricks for teaching in the cold. No prior outdoor learning experience needed! Great for those just starting out or those that have already been integrating outdoor learning into their teaching practices. Bring the family! Wolf Ridge provides daytime outdoor activities for youth (must be accompanied by an adult) or can recommend local spots for spring adventures. On Saturday evening, participants can experience Wolf Ridge’s outdoor adventure ropes course.

Great for those just starting out or those that have already been integrating outdoor learning into their teaching practices. Bring the family! Wolf Ridge provides daytime outdoor activities for youth (must be accompanied by an adult) or can recommend local spots for winter adventures. On Saturday evening, participants can experience Wolf Ridge’s outdoor adventure ropes course- the more snow, the better!

events.description: Please join Nagaajiwanaang Genawendangig Anishinaabemowin for Izhi-ganawendamang Gidinwewininaan Bapashkominitigong with Giizhibimi-ayaakwe miinawaa Niizhoodewin. We’ll talk about our experiences and different paths of learning as children and young adults, and the ways we integrate our passions for language learning and teaching into the Fond du Lac community through various work. We’ll also talk about the importance of this work and impacts it has had on our lives as young language speakers.

events.title: Spirit of the Wilderness Community Art Show, "The Art of Sabbath," Opening Reception
events.address: Johnson Heritage Post Art Gallery, 115 W. Wisconsin Street, Grand Marais, MN, 55604, United States
events.description: The Johnson Heritage Post Art Gallery is pleased to host the 15th annual Spirit of the Wilderness Community Art Show, themed "The Art of Sabbath." This gallery exhibition centers around winter in the north, which is a time of survival: physically, mentally, and spiritually. This exhibit explores how artists navigate the season, whether hibernating, ice fishing, or moving south, and looks at how we not only survive, but thrive, during the northern winter. Drawing on the ancient practice of Sabbath, participating artists showcase how they rest, recover, and restore through physical stillness and spiritual reconnection. The resulting works highlight these personal reflections across all mediums. The exhibit opens with a public reception on Friday, November 6, 2026, from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m., and runs through November 29, 2026.

events.title: Best Stargazing November
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: New moon nights – night when the moon is absent from the sky – make for great stargazing. Here’s a great way to start – look due north after the sun has set and find the Big Dipper constellation [see photo] with its telltale 3-star handle and 4-star dipper. In the autumn, the dipper is at ‘6-o’clock’ with the dipper facing up/handle to the left.

events.title: Taurids Meteor Shower
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: The Taurids meteor shower is an annual meteor shower that occurs every November and is composed of two streams, the Southern Taurids and the Northern Taurids. The Taurids are known for producing bright fireballs, and 2025 is predicted to be a year with an increased number of them At peak viewing times during the Taurid meteor shower, you may be able to see about a half-dozen shooting stars per hour. The Northern Taurids are active between Oct 20 - Dec 10 and peak on Nov. 9-12.

events.title: Leonids Meteor Shower
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: The Leonids meteor shower offers clear-sky meteor rates of about 10 to 15 shooting stars per hour. They are active between Nov. 6 - 30 and will peak on Nov. 17-18. The Leonids are bright meteors and have a high percentage of persistent trains according to AMS. The Leonids' radiant is located in the sickle-shaped head of the constellation Leo, the lion. Leonid meteor hunting can be incredible, or a total bust. It all depends on where its parent body, Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, will be in its orbit and the kind of debris clumps that will be around when our planet passes through this comet's orbit.

events.title: November Full Moon
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: 1st of 3 supermoons in a row A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. While the Frost Moon and Freezing Moon are self-explanatory, November's full moon is most known as the Beaver Moon. Beavers are quite active preparing for winter. Also known as the Mourning Moon, due to the increase in darkness.

events.title: Geminids Meteor Shower
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: The Geminids meteor shower occurs between November 19 to December 24 and this year will peak on the nights of December 13 and 14. The shower can produce 130 to 140 bright, white, fast meteors per hour on a clear sky. The debris that falls onto Earth's atmosphere during this meteor shower comes from the asteroid Phaethon. The meteor shower's radiant is located in the constellation Gemini, which rises around sunset.

events.title: December Full Moon
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: 2nd of 3 supermoons in a row A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. December's full moon is known as the Cold Moon or Long Nights Moon. In addition to the shortest daylight day of the year, the Long Nights Moon pertains to the amount of time the moon is above the horizon. It takes a high trajectory across the sky because it is opposite to the low sun.

events.title: January Full Moon
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: 3rd of 3 supermoons A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. The January full moon is most often known as the Wolf Moon because it is the month hungry wolves howl in the night. It is also known as the Stay Home, or Quiet, Moon as cold temps set in and we want to snuggle in and stay home.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Show Times are: November 5, 6, 7, 13 and 14 at 7:00pm Matinees November 8 and 15 at 2:00pm TICKET INFORMATION IS FOUND HERE.

events.description: This informative, entertaining Fe University course on the consecutive Tuesday afternoons of Nov. 10 and 17 in Mercer will teach you about the mammals, reptiles and amphibians that inhabit the Northwoods. events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Show Times are: November 5, 6, 7, 13 and 14 at 7:00pm Matinees November 8 and 15 at 2:00pm TICKET INFORMATION IS FOUND HERE.

events.title: Underground Critters: Herptiles and Mammals
events.description: This informative, entertaining Fe University course on the consecutive Tuesday afternoons of Nov. 10 and 17 in Mercer will teach you about the mammals, reptiles and amphibians that inhabit the Northwoods. Come away with a better understanding of how to identify these critters, where to find them, and how they survive conditions from harsh, cold winters to hot, dry summers. Hannah Thorpe will help you learn how to identify the reptiles and amphibians that share the Northwoods with us, their behavioral and physical adaptations, habitats, and ecology. With Jenna Malinowski, you’ll find out the important ecological roles small mammals such as rodents, bats, and lagomorphs play in conservation, and much more! Only $20 per person. Learn more and register at https://www.feuniversity.org/class/ ! Fe University: Jenna Malinowski and Hannah Thorpe – Underground Critters: Herptiles and Mammals Nov. 10 and 17, 2026, 1-2:30 p.m. Mercer Community Center, 2648W Margaret St., Mercer, Wis.

events.title: The Polar Express
events.description: Join us for our annual Frost Friday Family Film, this year featuring The Polar Express. Doors open at 6:30pm and movie starts at 7pm. Tickets are $8 for adults and $5 for students. Thank you to our movie sponsor: Wakefield Winter Wonderlights! Synopsis: On Christmas Eve, a skeptical young boy begins to doubt the existence of Santa Claus. Just before midnight, a mysterious steam train known as the Polar Express abruptly pulls up outside his home. Invited aboard by the enigmatic Conductor, he joins a group of other children on an extraordinary journey to the North Pole. Along the track, the children encounter daunting obstacles, strange wilderness figures, and moments that test their courage and friendship. Upon reaching the heart of Santa’s sprawling city, the young protagonist learns that the true magic of Christmas lies not in what you see, but in what you choose to believe—symbolized by a silver sleigh bell whose ring can only be heard by those who truly believe.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: Our Town
events.description: Theatre North Presents: Our Town, by Thornton Wilder, Directed by: Helen Fashbaugh Show Dates and Times: February 18, 19, 20, 26 and 27 at 7:00pm Matinees February 21 and 28 at 2:00pm Thornton Wilder’s American classic, Pultizer-prize winning Our Town, explores the universal human experience of life, love, and death. Set in the fictional small town of Grover’s Corners, New Hampshire, the story follows the everyday lives of the Gibbs and Webb families across three acts. The play is famous for its minimalist approach, often performed on a bare stage with no curtains or scenery, relying on pantomime and a narrator called the Stage Manager to guide the audience into its intimacy and truth. The narrative is divided into three distinct acts: Act I: Daily Life: Introduces the town’s routine, highlighting the simple chores, gossip, and rhythms of small-town life. Act II: Love and Marriage: Follows the childhood friends, George Gibbs and Emily Webb, as they fall in love, grow up, and get married. Act III: Death and Eternity: Concludes years later with Emily’s tragic death in childbirth.

events.title: ACLARA Meeting
events.description: Aitkin County Lakes and Rivers Association (aka ACLARA) represents 20 lake associations in Aitkin County. Founded in 2005, ACLARA brings together lake/river associations throughout Aitkin County for the purpose of educating members on keeping its lakes/rivers and shore land healthy for future generations. Meetings are held on the second Saturday, April through October, usually at the Aitkin County Library stating at 9:30 a.m. Members are encouraged to discuss their association’s issues, if any, and share ideas on lake/river management, water quality and conservation matters that impact the waters we all appreciate and enjoy. Communication to the membership is via email. Annual, nonrefundable dues are $25 for one representative and one or two alternates. Dues cover the costs of any pertinent information to keep members informed on important issues, local expert speakers on a variety of topics at the monthly meetings and minimal administrative costs. Individuals who share a common interest in the well-being of our lakes/rivers and are not part of an active lake/river association may also join annually for $25.

events.title: Jill D. Swenson: Exploring Land, Loss, and Legacy
events.description: Author Talk | Jill D. Swenson | Exploring Land, Loss, and Legacy Wednesday, November 4, 5:30 - 6:30 p.m. Grand Marais Public Library Free, open to all Set in the Lake of the Woods region of northern Minnesota, Jill D. Swenson’s memoir, The Land of Everlasting Sky: A Memoir of Loss and Legacy on Lake of the Woods, brings together family history, personal grief, and questions of land, identity, and belonging. After returning to her mother’s hometown following her death, Swenson begins investigating the region’s history and the experiences of the descendants of Kakaygeesick, an Ojibway spiritual leader. Her research leads to a friendship with Kakaygeesick’s great-grandson and a deeper examination of land allotment, tribal membership, and federal Indian policy. As she explores these histories, Swenson also confronts the losses and family estrangements that have shaped her own life. Both personal and historical in scope, The Land of Everlasting Sky considers how the past continues to influence our understanding of ourselves, our communities, and our relationships to the land. Books will be available for purchase at the event through Drury Lane Books. Jill D.

events.title: Northern Lotus Meditation
events.description: Meditation can be a path to self-awareness and compassion toward others, but it can also be a path to better overall health and well-being, mentally, emotionally, and physically. Experience a mindful group meditation practice in a warm and inclusive environment. Whether you're a seasoned meditator or a complete beginner, all are welcome. No prior experience is needed; just an open heart and a willingness to explore this path. With Rev. Zahir Orest EVERY WEDNESDAY 7:00 - 8:00 pm If you're new, arrive at 6:45 for meditation instructions. 7:00 – 7:20 Sitting meditation 7:20 – 7:30 Walking breath practice (Kinhin) 7:30 – 7:50 Sitting meditation 7:50 – 8:00 Formal Exit You are welcome to join in either or both of the sitting meditations. Floor cushions and chairs are provided. Free-will donations are much appreciated. Contact Rev. Zahir Roman Orest at (612) 865-4369 for more information or with any questions. Recurring weekly on Wednesday.

events.title: Date Night in the Barrel Room
events.description: Join us for a Date Night in the Barrel Room at North Shore Winery! We are open late on Thursdays, so grab your date and come down to the winery for music from 6:00 to 8:00 pm featuring fingerstyle guitar master and highly regarded bluesman Gordon Thorne. Gordon Thorne picked up a guitar 30 years ago and hasn’t put it down since. He spent years mining early American blues and jazz, blending them with his own style, and serves up what he calls, “the modern sounds of yesterday – today.” Known as the meanest fingerpicker in Northern Minnesota it is where he spends his time working, raising kids and playing a little guitar. Recurring weekly on Thursday.

events.title: Storytime at the Library
events.description: Storytime at the Library Grand Marais Public Library - 10:30 AM October 29 November 12, 19 December 3, 10, 17 The Grand Marais Public Library is excited to welcome families back for a brand-new season of Storytime. This free program is designed for preschool-aged children. Each Storytime session combines engaging picture books with a fun, hands-on activity designed to support children’s early learning and development. Children will practice important readiness skills such as vocabulary development, phonological awareness, active listening, and taking turns. Older children who attend with a younger sibling or friend will also have an alternative activity available. After the stories, families are invited to enjoy a simple craft designed to strengthen fine motor skills. Before heading home, be sure to stop by the library’s children’s section and choose a fresh bundle of books to take home and enjoy together! We look forward to seeing you at Storytime this season! Recurring weekly on Thursday.

events.title: Spirit of the Wilderness Community Art Show, "The Art of Sabbath," Opening Reception
events.description: The Johnson Heritage Post Art Gallery is pleased to host the 15th annual Spirit of the Wilderness Community Art Show, themed "The Art of Sabbath." The exhibit opens with a public reception on Friday, November 6, 2026, from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m., and runs through November 29, 2026. This gallery exhibition centers around winter in the north, which is a time of survival: physically, mentally, and spiritually. This exhibit explores how artists navigate the season, whether hibernating, ice fishing, or moving south, and looks at how we not only survive, but thrive, during the northern winter. Drawing on the ancient practice of Sabbath, participating artists showcase how they rest, recover, and restore through physical stillness and spiritual reconnection. The resulting works highlight these personal reflections across all mediums.

events.title: Economic Development Authority Public Hearing - Sale of Property
events.address: City Hall Council Chambers, 600 4th St, International Falls, MN 56649
events.description: In accordance with Minnesota Statute 469.105, Subd. 2, theInternational Falls’ Economic Development Authority will hold a Public Hearingon Monday, November 23, 2026 at the hour of 4:00 P.M. in the Council Chambersof the International Falls Municipal Building, 600 4th Street, InternationalFalls, Minnesota. The purpose for the public hearing is to provide taxpayersthe opportunity to testify for or against the sale of the following parcels ofland (the “Property”) to Onesimus, Corporation: 92-060-44100 and 22-036-31100. The EDA will meet at the public hearing to determine if thesale is advisable. A copy of the termsand conditions of the proposed sale of the Property will be on file andavailable for inspection at City Hall during regular business hours. Any person wishing to express an opinion onthe matters to be considered at the public hearing will be heard orally or inwriting. For more information, contact the authority office at (218)283-9484, or visit their offices located at City Hall, International FallsMunicipal Building, 600 4 th Street, International Falls, Minnesota.

events.title: Live Music: Balterdash
events.description: Balterdash is Sue Orfield (tenor sax & vocals), Dustin DeGolier (guitars & vocals), John Utphall (keys, fiddle & vocals), and Randy Sinz (basses & vocals) We take great pride in performing our original songs, mixed in with unique arrangements of carefully selected cover tunes. Our sound is a rich fusion of Bluegrass, Americana, and Celtic influences, creating a vibrant and engaging musical experience that resonates with a wide range of listeners. Sue Orfield is an award winning tenor saxophonist, composer and educator who tours internationally and has recorded on hundreds of albums. She makes her home in the Chippewa Valley of Wisconsin. Over the years Sue has shared the stage with many musical greats, among them Bo Diddley, Bobby McFerrin, The Indigo Girls, Ann Wilson (Heart), Dizzy Gillespie, Ivan Neville, and Jo Dee Messina. Dustin DeGolier is a freelance musician serving Northwest Wisconsin. A native of Cumberland, WI, Dustin maintains a frequent performance schedule both solo and with a wide array of groups playing jazz, rock, Americana, blues and more.

events.title: Veterans Day Program
events.description: Join the Spooner Area School District on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, at 9:45 AM in the High School Gymnasium for a special Veterans Day Program honoring the brave men and women who have served our country. Community members, families, and veterans are warmly invited to come together for this meaningful tribute as we recognize the service, courage, and sacrifices of our nation's heroes. All veterans are welcome and encouraged to attend! Refreshments will be served in the high school media center following the program. Come together as a community to honor, thank, and remember those who have served!

events.title: 127th Christmas Bird Count
events.description: Hunt Hill Nature Center will be hosting the National Audubon Society's 127th Christmas Bird Count on Saturday, December 19, 2026. This event is the longest running citizen science program in the world. Volunteers will be assigned routes to travel within the Long Lake/ Birchwood area to count the birds they see on their route. This program is open to all levels of birding experience and ability. Citizen Science empowers the curious and concerned to collect valuable data that contributes to specific scientific research. Volunteers should meet at Hunt Hill Nature Center at 7:45 am. Registration Required by December 17, 2026. Register on line or by calling 715-635-6543.

events.title: A Play: Walter Cronkite is Dead
events.description: THE STORY : A fierce thunderstorm has shut down airports up and down the East Coast. Two women, who appear to have nothing in common, are stuck in a waiting area at Reagan National Airport. Patty is a chatty southerner—a blue-collar woman from a red state—who is almost physically unable to tolerate silence. Margaret is a Washingtonian, reserved, educated, liberal and not interested in sharing her thoughts, or her table, with Patty. Forced together for a long night in a public place, the two strangers have no choice but to share a bottle of wine and begin to talk...and to listen. Their conversation is funny, difficult, deeply revealing and astonishingly frank. Patty and Margaret share details of their lives that lead them to a place of kinship neither of them could have imagined. Yes, Walter Cronkite is dead, but his wisdom and compassion lives on in this insightful comedy about what might be possible if people from opposite sides of the political aisle would stop shouting and take even one night to listen.

events.title: The Initials Game Live
events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.title: Introduction to Designing & Building Cutting and Charcuterie Boards
events.description: Create Your Own Hardwood Charcuterie Board in Hurley Nov. 7-8 Here’s an introductory course for anyone who wants to learn how to work with hardwoods and has little or no knowledge of the process. In the Fe University course “Introduction to Designing and Building Cutting and Charcuterie Boards,” spend a concentrated weekend Nov. 7-8 in the Hurley High School Woods Shop from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. learning from Fine Woodworking instructor Tim Lutgen how to work with mixed hardwoods, lay out your project, select the best wood, perform all machining under experienced guidance, and finish your custom creation. Show off your own beautiful hardwood creation to family and friends, or even gift it to loved ones this holiday season! Registration is $45, which does not include the cost of materials. Space is limited, so don’t wait! Learn more and sign up at FeUniversity.org. Questions about registration? Call 715-862-2032 or 715-476-2881.

events.title: Lakeside Yoga Stretch
events.description: Admission $12.00 Location NLDC Lodge or Amphitheater Description Wherever you are in your yoga practice, this class is for you. Lakeside Yoga is a gently paced class that encourages deep release in the body's major muscle groups. Through mindful stretching, breathwork, and intentional movement, students can increase flexibility, ease chronic pain, and improve their overall range of motion. Lakeside Yoga also helps build strength and cultivates balance in both body and mind. Whether you're new to yoga or a seasoned practitioner, you'll leave feeling grounded, refreshed, and restored. All are welcome. Class will be held at the Discovery Center indoors. We suggest participants bring a yoga mat and water. Class will be held at the Discovery Center in the Main Lodge or the Ampitheater (weather dependent). All levels welcome. Charge for each class is $12.00 to be paid on the day of class. No registration required. Saturday 9:30 AM - 10:30 AM. Registration is not required for yoga and takes place weekly. We do not allow the ability to register online in advance, as payment is taken at the door. Please be prepared to pay $12.00 on the day of class.

events.title: Underground Critters: Herptiles & Mammals
events.description: Meet the Underground Critters of the Northwoods Nov. 10 & 17 Critters are all around us here in the Northwoods – some much less visible, although no less vital, than others. On the consecutive Tuesday afternoons of Nov. 10 and 17, from 1 to 2:30 p.m. in Mercer, come learn about the mammals, reptiles and amphibians that inhabit the Northwoods in the Fe University course “Underground Critters: Herptiles and Mammals” with Jenna Malinowski and Hannah Thorpe. You’ll come away with a better understanding of how to identify these critters, where to find them, and how they survive conditions from harsh, cold winters to hot, dry summers. $20. Learn traditional methods, modern techniques, and simple recipes you can try at home. No experience needed. We’ll wrap up on the porch to sample the results and enjoy some cold beverages. Come hungry, you’ll leave full! Space is limited to 20 participants, so sign up early to join us for this laid-back, flavorful experience! Registration required by 11/8/26. Tuesday, November 10th, 5:00 PM - 7:00 PM. $60/Non-Member and $48/Member. Please read our program and event registration and cancellation policy here.

events.title: Natural Pages: The Death and Life of the Great Lakes by Dan Egan
events.description: A partnership between the Discovery Center and Koller Library, each month we will focus on a different nature-based book each month, with discussions led by either Discovery Center or library staff. Books will be available for checkout at the library in the weeks prior to the meeting. The Great Lakes--Erie, Huron, Michigan, Ontario, and Superior--hold 20 percent of the world's supply of surface fresh water and provide sustenance, work, and recreation for tens of millions of Americans. But they are under threat as never before, and their problems are spreading across the continent. The Death and Life of the Great Lakes is prize-winning reporter Dan Egan's compulsively readable portrait of an ecological catastrophe happening right before our eyes, blending the epic story of the lakes with an examination of the perils they face and the ways we can restore and preserve them for generations to come. This event is free and open to the public. Registration is not required but is appreciated. This month's Natural Pages Reading Group gathering will be held at the Koller Library in Manitowish Waters. Tuesday, November 10th, 5:00 PM - 6:00 PM.

events.title: Nibbles n’ Knowledge: Hidden Moose of Wisconsin: Uncovering Wisconsin’s Resident Moose
events.description: For more than a decade, Amanda Griggs has documented hundreds of moose observations across northern Wisconsin, revealing a story that challenges long-held assumptions about the species. Through photographs, trail camera images, field research, and individual stories like the well-known bull "Pancho," participants will explore the evidence supporting Wisconsin's resident moose population and learn how citizen science has contributed to a greater understanding of these elusive animals. The presentation also highlights ongoing conservation efforts and how the public can become involved in monitoring and protecting Wisconsin's moose. We will serve light appetizers and have a cash bar from 5:00 PM - 6:00 PM, presentation will run from 6:00 PM - 7:00 PM. Registration required by 11/10/26. Program is held at the North Lakeland Discovery Center Main Lodge. $17/Non-Member, $14/Member and $20 at the door for anyone who has not pre-registered. Thursday, November 12th, 5:00 PM - 7:00 PM. events.title: Soldiers of the American Revolution - Lake of the Woods School, hosted by Baudette Public Library
events.description: The Arrowhead Library System is pleased to present Soldiers of the American Revolution with Arn Kind of Historical Experiences. These free history events will travel to participating ALS libraries October 14-November 20, 2026. On this 250th Anniversary of the Declaration of Independence join Arn Kind for an event all about the American Revolution. This in depth presentation puts audience members into the life of a revolutionary soldier with historical artifacts, uniforms, and hands-on experiences. Audiences will enjoy learning about the causes of the revolution and how it led to the birth of the United States of America. This two hour program is suited for ages 10 and up. These free programs are being offered at the following locations: Wednesday, October 14, 1:00 p.m. - 3:00 p.m. - Coleraine Public Library Thursday, October 15, 10:00 a.m. - 12:00 p.m. - Marble Public Library Thursday, October 15, 4:00 p.m. - 6:00 p.m. - Calumet Public Library Friday, October 16, 1:00 p.m. - 3:00 p.m. - Buhl Public Library Saturday, October 17, 10:00 a.m. - 12:00 p.m. - Eveleth Public Library Monday, October 19, 10:00 a.m. - 12:00 p.m. - Cook Public Library Tuesday, October 20, 10:00 a.m.

events.title: Cataloging Workday
events.description: Cataloging Workday Tuesday, November 24, 2026 – 10:00 to3:00 In Person at ALS Audience: Horizon and BLUEcloud Catalogers with questions Description: ALS catalogers assemble to offer expertise and advice during a day of work! This session will focus on special topics and questions staff have about any aspect of cataloging, brainstorming common issues, and some discussion of cataloging standards across the ALS system. We will be working on cataloging items, so bring up to 15 items and questions to go with them. We suggest bringing a few special items like kits or "library of things" items to discuss, and there will be access to OCLC records. There will be a half hour brown bag lunch/break at noon, and attendees can come and go as they please. Note: if possible, please bring any laptops or relevant tech to help you work. In order to address issues equitably, please only bring up to 15 examples you’d like us to work on.

events.title: Music Then and Now Concert: Virginia Public Library
events.description: Free Solo String Concerts to tour local ALS libraries this November and December The Arrowhead Library System is pleased to present free concerts at participating ALS libraries November 17 - December 18, 2026. This music event, presented by musician Sara Pajunen, is titled: Music Then and Now: a Solo String Concert . Join Sara Pajunen on a tour of classical, folk, and original music on violin and hardanger d'amore, a ten-string bow instrument. This concert showcases Sara's musical repertoire and original compositions, inspired by travels abroad and grounded in her childhood on the Iron Range. This program is 50 minutes long and suited for adults and children of all ages. These free programs are being offered at the following locations: Tuesday, November 17, 1:00 p.m. - Ely Public Library Wednesday, November 18, 6:30 p.m. - International Falls Public Library Thursday, November 19, 10:00 a.m. - CHI Lakewood Care Center, hosted by Baudette Public Library Friday, November 20, 10:00 a.m. - Mountain Iron Public Library Friday, November 20, 3:30 p.m. - Buhl Public Library Saturday, November 21, 10:00 a.m. - Eveleth Public Library Wednesday, December 2, 10:00 a.m.

events.title: Ian Alexy
events.description: Troubadour 21st Century is the new record by singer-songwriter Ian Alexy. Best known for his work with Americana duo Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank, Ian expands the possibilities on Troubadour 21st Century with rock grooves and spine-tingling electric guitar flourishes. This is Ian Alexy’s fifth album as a solo artist, in addition to five albums with Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank. Hobo Nephews first earned their live reputation by opening a sold-out national tour for Trampled By Turtles before touring all over the United States as a headliner. Their 2015 song Old Number 4 was featured on CBS Sports.com and soon after went viral. Ian has received critical acclaim for his work as a solo artist as well. In addition to performing as a solo artist and with his band Ian Alexy and The Deserters, he is also working on a series of documentaries titled Making It Shine comprised of footage of life on the road and in the studio over the past several years. With the world re opening again the Troubadour 21st Century is ready to return to the music life. “Invokes 80s era Petty and Springsteen.” - Minneapolis Star Tribune “Stomping Blues Rock reminiscent of Dan Auerbach.”

events.title: 38 Special
events.description: After more than four decades together, 38 SPECIAL continues to bring their signature blast of Southern Rock to over 100 cities a year. And at each and every show, thousands of audience members are amazed by the explosive power of the band's performance. Their many Gold and Platinum album awards stand in testament to the endurance of a legendary powerhouse. With sales in excess of 20 million, most associate the band with their arena-rock pop smashes, “Hold On Loosely,” “Rockin’ Into the Night,” “Caught Up in You,” “Fantasy Girl,” “If I’d Been the One,” “Back Where You Belong,” “Chain Lightnin’,” “Second Chance,” and more – Timeless hits that remain a staple at radio, immediately recognizable from the first opening chord, and paving the way to their present-day touring regimen.

events.title: 38 Special
events.description: 38 Special is an American rock band. Formed by Guitarist/Vocalist Don Barnes and vocalist Donnie Van Zant in 1974 in Jacksonville, Florida, the band initially had a straight-ahead Southern rock sound, much like Lynyrd Skynyrd, the band of Donnie's older brother Ronnie. By the early 1980s, the band began incorporating elements of blues-rock and arena rock into their sound, kicking off a string of successful albums and singles. Among 38 Special's best-known songs are "Caught Up in You" (1982) and "If I'd Been the One" (1983), both of which hit #1 on Billboard magazine's album rock chart, and "Second Chance" (1989), a #1 hit on Billboard's adult contemporary chart. Their other hit singles include "Hold On Loosely" (1981) and "Back Where You Belong" (1984). The band is comprised of guitarist/vocalist Don Barnes, guitarist Jerry Riggs, bassist Barry Dunaway, keyboardist Bobby Capps, and drummer Gary Moffatt.

events.title: Lee Clark Allen
events.description: Three Bands - Three Cool Vibes Lee Clark Allen is an independent singer-songwriter, instrumentalist, and producer whose music bridges the timeless warmth of classic soul with the contemporary edge of modern R&B. Rooted in live instrumentation, his sound blends elements of jazz, blues, rock, funk, gospel, pop, and hip-hop to create something both fresh and familiar. Allen crafts music that is as rich in musicianship as it is in storytelling. His debut EP, Little Rock, introduced his signature style of smooth, groove-driven melodies paired with introspective, heartfelt lyrics. With his released LP, My World Is Yours, Allen expands his sonic palette, showcasing deeper textures and a refined approach to songwriting and production. His sound is built on authenticity, utilizing real instruments, real stories, and real emotion. Teague Alexy
events.description: Award-winning Duluth-based musician, author and storyteller Teague Alexy is probably best known for his Americana songwriting in the national touring brothers duo Hobo Nephews of Uncle Frank. Teague’s songwriting is clearly influenced by his home in Minnesota, as well as his childhood in New Jersey, and life as a travelling musical hobo. Teague's storytelling has deeper roots to his Irish ancestry. The name ‘Teague’ was once used to describe the storytelling poets who travelled ancient Ireland. New album "Effervescent" available 2/14/16. Teague's second album of 2017 is a collaboration with Trampled By Turtles mandolin player Erik Berry. 'Irish American' features nine traditional Irish favorites, including "Whiskey in the Jar," "The Wild Colonial Boy" and "Mountain Dew," as well as two original songs. Teague’s first album of 2017, Circuit Sessions, combines multiple musical genres into a powerful new collection of Teague’s poetic songs with the lionstrong production and rhythm section of Eric Pollard (Actual Wolf) and Steve Garrington (Low) joined by Minneapolis guitarist Jake Hanson. Teague also has a new musical and storytelling podcast “Wisecracks & Roadside Flats.”

Styx
events.description: The six men comprising STYX have committed to rocking the Paradise together with audiences far and wide by averaging over 100 shows a year every year since (yes) 1999, and each one of them is committed to making the next show better than the last. Founded in Chicago in 1972, STYX has the unique distinction of being the first band in rock history to have four consecutive certified multimillion-selling albums in a row: 1977’s The Grand Illusion, 1978’s Pieces of Eight, 1979’s Cornerstone, and 1981’s Paradise Theatre. STYX draws from over four decades of barnburning chart hits, joyous singalongs, and harddriving deep cuts. Like a symphony that builds to a satisfying crescendo, a STYX set covers a wide range of stylistic cornerstones.

events.title: Amy Speace
events.description: A tour celebrating the launch of Amy's debut book of poetry, "The Cardinals" (Red Hen Press). She will be singing and reading selections from the book, which will be on sale at the show. Heralded by Rolling Stone, Billboard Magazine and The New York Times and featured on NPR’s “All Things Considered”, Amy Speace was discovered by Judy Collins, who signed her to her record label and has recorded her songs. She’s the 2020 winner of the AMA UK’s International Song of the Year. Her newest record, “The American Dream,” was released October 18th and became the #1 record and the title track was named #1 song in the FAI Radio Charts for its first month out. Her song, “The Weight of the World” was named the #4 record of last decade by WFUV, NYC. As well, her song, “The Sea and the Shore” was named as one of the 100 best folk songs of the era. She will be releasing a single of Woody Guthrie’s “Plane Wreck at Los Gatos” this summer accompanied by a video, to help raise awareness for the ACLU. A writer’s writer, her forthcoming debut collection of poetry will be published by Red Hen Press in Spring 2027.

events.title: Styx
events.description: Tommy Shaw, James “JY” Young, Lawrence Gowan, Todd Sucherman, Will Evankovich, and Terry Gowan (along with the occasional surprise appearance by original bassist Chuck Panozzo), have performed more live since ’99 than all of the previous years of its career combined. Two Super-Bowl appearances, Pollstar Box Office chart-topping tours with Def Leppard, Journey, Boston, REO Speedwagon, Bad Company (to name only a few), two more studio albums and no end in sight, STYX continues to conquer the planet, one venue at a time. Spawned from a suburban Chicago basement in the early ‘70s, Styx would eventually transform into the virtual arena rock prototype by the late '70s and early '80s, due to a fondness for big rockers and soaring power ballads. Early on, Styx's music reflected such then-current prog rockers as Emerson, Lake & Palmer and the Moody Blues, as evidenced by such releases as 1972's self-titled debut, 1973's Styx II, 1974's The Serpent Is Rising, and 1975's Man of Miracles.

events.title: #IMOMSOHARD
events.description: This summer, Jen and Kristin from #IMOMSOHARD are taking their show out of the playroom and onto the road. But this time, they’re bringing the kids. And a tour bus (you didn’t think they’d leave them with their husbands, did you?). There’s no one making moms feel as uncomfortably normal as Kristin Hensley and Jen Smedley, the hilarious oh-so-real women behind #IMomSoHard. With over 675,000 Facebook fans, and more than 55 million views of their web series, Jen and Kristin’s blend of honesty and humor offer the kinds of levity most of us only get from our therapist, proving that if we weren’t all laughing, we’d be crying, right? Right!? Sure to deliver the kind of straight talk you can only get from discussing body hair in the kids’ playroom while sipping mimosas, Kristin and Jen prove you can’t make this shi*t up. It’s like an evening with two of your besties. But funnier. And probably with more drinking.

events.title: Becky Kapell Music: Rich Mattson & Germaine Gemberling with Becky Kapell & Paul Bergen
events.venue: Cedar Lounge - Earth Rider Brewery taproom

events.description: Gary Owen has been entertaining audiences for more than two decades with his sharp observational humor and fearless storytelling. Known for his unapologetic, rule-defying style, his material draws from his personal life, time in the military and the everyday absurdities that connect people across backgrounds. With a fanbase that has grown by the millions in recent months and continues to surge across social media, Owen’s reach has cemented his place as one of the most in-demand touring comedians today. Beyond stand-up, Owen has appeared in a wide range of feature films including BACK ON THE STRIP with Tiffany Haddish and Wesley Snipes, MEET THE BLACKS and its sequel THE HOUSE NEXT DOOR, THINK LIKE A MAN and THINK LIKE A MAN TOO, RIDE ALONG with Ice Cube and Kevin Hart, LITTLE MAN opposite the Wayans Brothers, and DADDY DAY CARE with Eddie Murphy. He is also widely recognized for his scene-stealing role as “Bearcat” in the MGM film COLLEGE. On television, Owen starred in his own BET series THE GARY OWEN SHOW and co-hosted TruTV’s sketch series UPLOAD WITH SHAQUILLE O’NEAL.

events.title: John Louis
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Country troubadour John Louis wanders around this world of music, writing and singing heartworn country folk songs. John’s that guy on the bus who sits quietly, looking tired like the rest of us. The difference is he is sitting there composing a song about your life and those painful poignant moments you dust off on the way home between life’s chores. His songs show us our lives and the subtle but important things that become universally important hallmarks of our Midwestern journey. Like church basement rolls at the funeral. Like the small moments on road trips filled with meaning, loss and memory. The tragedies and triumphs that break us and keep us going one more day. John glimpses it all through a poet’s heart. When he stands bravely on a stage with a guitar and begins singing, we get to see it too. And it makes sense for a moment. The songs John writes keep winning awards from prestigious songwriting showcases. Including the Kerrville Folk Festival New Folk competition, Rocky Mountain Folks Festival Songwriter Showcase, and the Great River Folk Fest songwriter contest. (That’s some hot sh-t folks!)

events.description: John Kerns John Kerns is a dynamic musician who brings a fresh and unique approach to live performance. With a deep catalog of original songs and an extensive repertoire of covers, he crafts engaging and immersive musical experiences that keep audiences hooked from start to finish. Using guitar, percussion stomp boxes, looping pedals and a telephone microphone, John layers sounds to create the energy and depth of a full band—all created live on the spot. Whether playing an intimate venue or a festival, Kerns’ music is always inventive and captivating. His ability to blend rhythm, melody, and texture builds rich, layered soundscapes that leave audiences cheering and wanting more.

events.title: The Oak Ridge Boys
events.description: Theirs has been one of the most distinctive and timeless sounds in the music industry for over 50 years, and now The Oak Ridge Boys are bringing their Celebrating Route 66 tour across the country for an unforgettable night of entertainment for the entire family. The show will feature many of the group's country hits and two pop smashes, songs that earned them Grammy, Dove, CMA, and ACM awards, as well as garnering a host of other industry and fan accolades. "When I go on stage, I get the same feeling I had the first time I sang with The Oak Ridge Boys," says lead singer Duane Allen. "This is the only job I've ever wanted to have." "'Elvira' was always on repeat when I was growing up," says tenor Ben James. "It's still one of those timeless songs that never grow old." James first met The Oak Ridge Boys in November 2022. "Joe (Bonsall) handed me the mic and said, 'You've got the next verse,'" James said. "I'm not sure I will ever get over that moment." A little more than a year later, Bonsall handed the microphone to James permanently, announcing his retirement from the group in January of 2024. Bonsall passed away several months later due to complications from ALS.

events.description: Barron Ryan’s love for music has always been divided. The son of two musicians, he grew up in a house filled with the sounds of everything ranging from Beethoven to James Brown. So when it comes to his own performing, he’s not content drawing on just one of those influences; he combines them all into an adventure that’s vintage yet fresh, historical yet hip, classic yet cool. Even when beginning to make his own music, Barron needed more than one outlet. He started piano lessons at the age of four, but at the same time began teaching himself drums. While progressing through middle and high schools, he won prizes in classical piano competitions while also earning a reputation as a formidable jazz drummer. In college, Barron continued to excel in multiple fields, majoring in piano performance and even earning a spot playing snare in the marching band drumline. Though he increasingly turned his focus toward the piano, the genres of classical, jazz, and funk continued to attract his attention. Now Barron applies his myriad interests and expertise to create an awe-inspiring program.

events.description: J Streitz plays original Midwest Americana music. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Along with his band, Shane has earned recognition as one of the Northland’s top local musical acts by winning several battle of the bands competitions, being voted the Northland’s best live musical act by local radio stations, and through live performances throughout the Midwest. events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description: Mason Jennings is a Minnesota-based pop-folk singer-songwriter. Jennings is originally from Honolulu, Hawaii. He is well known for his simple yet catchy melodies, intimate lyrics, intensely literary and historical themes, and deep tenor's voice. His music has appeared in the surf film Shelter and he has toured extensively. Jennings is married to Amy Jennings (nee Turany) and has a son, August, born in January 2003. Jennings produced his self-titled debut album in 1997 on an analog four-track in the basement of a rented home, manning all instruments himself. In October 1998, after bringing drummer Chris Stock and bassist Robert Skoro on board, he began a weekly gig at Minneapolis' 400 Bar as the Mason Jennings Band. Garnering local praise and a wide fan base, Mason began touring nationally. His 2000 album Birds Flying Away revealed Jennings' political activism and penchant for singing first-person narratives of imaginary rustic characters. Following the release of this album, Noah Levy took over drumming duties from Stock. 2002 saw the release of two albums: the studio piece Century Spring and a "fans only" collection of acoustic rarities, Simple Life.

events.description: Dead North is a progressive bluegrass band from the northwoods of Michigan’s Keweenaw Peninsula. Now residing in Minneapolis, the band is composed of Luke Pascot (guitar, vocals, banjo) and Kora Melia (mandolin, fiddle, vocals). Together, they push the limits of the bluegrass genre with bold experimentation while still maintaining a high level of respect for tradition. Their sound elegantly mixes bluegrass with elements of jazz, rock, country, funk, and so much more. Influenced by the likes of Tony Rice, Billy Strings, David Grisman, etc., Dead North is a must see for any fans of progressive acoustic music. Death Valley Yacht Club's signature sound features their intricate vocal harmonies sung over the interplay between their tightly-arranged acoustic guitars. MN Songbird described the band's sound as “timeless”, saying they could imagine hearing the music “in the 90’s opening for someone like Elliott Smith.” Their original music takes inspiration from artists like The Beatles, Neil Young, The Avett Brothers, and Jesse Welles.

events.title: John Louis
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Country troubadour John Louis wanders around this world of music, writing and singing heartworn country folk songs. John’s that guy on the bus who sits quietly, looking tired like the rest of us. The difference is he is sitting there composing a song about your life and those painful poignant moments you dust off on the way home between life’s chores. His songs show us our lives and the subtle but important things that become universally important hallmarks of our Midwestern journey. Like church basement rolls at the funeral. Like the small moments on road trips filled with meaning, loss and memory. The tragedies and triumphs that break us and keep us going one more day. John glimpses it all through a poet’s heart. When he stands bravely on a stage with a guitar and begins singing, we get to see it too. And it makes sense for a moment. The songs John writes keep winning awards from prestigious songwriting showcases. Including the Kerrville Folk Festival New Folk competition, Rocky Mountain Folks Festival Songwriter Showcase, and the Great River Folk Fest songwriter contest. (That’s some hot sh-t folks!)

events.description: 20 years is a long time to spend doing anything at all. It’s an age for any group of people to sustain a collective effort. For a band on the road, 20 years can be more than a lifetime. Yet, after 2 decades of making music together in living rooms, listening rooms, clubs, theaters, and festival stages, The Steel Wheels are still growing, still pushing, still at it, and they’re marking the occasion with the release of their 9th studio album, “The Steel Wheels”. Following the release of “Sideways” in 2024, their 3rd record with producer Sam Kassirer at his Great North Sound Society studio in interior Maine, the band felt it was time for a change of scene. As the group began to select songs for a new album, they also had to find an answer to the question of where they would get down to the work of record-making. They didn’t know that answer was going to knock on their back door. At the band’s 2024 Red Wing Roots festival, held each summer near the group’s home base of Harrisonburg, VA, banjo player and songwriter Trent Wagler spied producer and engineer D.

events.title: Teague Alexy
events.description: Award-winning Duluth-based musician, author and storyteller Teague Alexy is probably best known for his Americana songwriting in the national touring brothers duo Hobo Nephews of Uncle Frank. Teague’s songwriting is clearly influenced by his home in Minnesota, as well as his childhood in New Jersey, and life as a travelling musical hobo. Teague's storytelling has deeper roots to his Irish ancestry. The name ‘Teague’ was once used to describe the storytelling poets who travelled ancient Ireland. New album "Effervescent" available 2/14/16. Teague's second album of 2017 is a collaboration with Trampled By Turtles mandolin player Erik Berry. 'Irish American' features nine traditional Irish favorites, including "Whiskey in the Jar," "The Wild Colonial Boy" and "Mountain Dew," as well as two original songs. Teague’s first album of 2017, Circuit Sessions, combines multiple musical genres into a powerful new collection of Teague’s poetic songs with the lionstrong production and rhythm section of Eric Pollard (Actual Wolf) and Steve Garrington (Low) joined by Minneapolis guitarist Jake Hanson. Teague also has a new musical and storytelling podcast “Wisecracks & Roadside Flats.”

events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz | The Ore House
events.description: J Streitz plays original folk/Americana songs along with a few covers by great songwriters including John Prine, Todd Snider, and Bob Dylan. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album. The bones of album #2 were recorded in June of 2019 at The Hideaway Studios in NE Minneapolis and is set to be released in the Winter of 2021.

events.title: The New Standards Holiday Show ~ Duluth, MN
events.description: The New Standards Holiday Show features the trio as wise-cracking hosts of a seasonal spectacle that's just Christmasy enough. With a little help from their friends, The New Standards warms the hearts of the grinchiest of grinches in what has become an enduring, and endearing, Minnesota holiday tradition. Minnesota stalwarts The New Standards create an intriguing blend of everything from classic cabaret to punk rock, from the freedom of jazz, to the soul of pop and rock. They make it work through sheer musicianship and offbeat humor. The instrumentation is simple: John Munson of Trip Shakespeare/Semisonic fame on bass; Chan Poling, founder of the new-wave group The Suburbs on piano; and Steve Roehm on vibes. Chan and John split the singing. A foot stomp here, a shout-out, a fiery solo, and it's cooked. Simple, elegant, illuminating.

events.title: Davina and The Vagabonds: A Vagabond Holiday
events.description: Davina and the Vagabonds bring a signature high-energy blend of blues, neo-soul, and swing to the winter season with their annual "A Vagabond Holiday" shows and festive recordings. Known for frontwoman Davina Sowers' distinctively soulful vocals and a heavy brass presence, the Twin Cities-based group frequently hits the road each winter. New Spin on an Old Sound Davina and the Vagabonds are playing your area soon! Davina Sowers and the Vagabonds have created a stir on the national music scene with their high-energy live shows, level A musicianship, sharp-dressed professionalism, and Sowers’ commanding stage presence. With influences ranging from Fats Domino and the Preservation Hall Jazz Band to Aretha Franklin and Tom Waits, the band is converting audiences one show at a time, from Vancouver to Miami and across Europe. In 2011 Davina released her first full length, all original album Black Cloud . It was named one of the 10 best releases of the year by the Minneapolis Star & Tribune and awarded 4 1⁄2 stars from Downbeat Magazine.

events.description: Join us on a frozen night in December as we wake the city up from it's hibernation. Hometown hero's Pronoya come back in town and they brought some friends. Shadows of me, Xkwizite, Kalopsya, and Druid are all coming together at the Caddyshack indoor golf course on December 11th. It is a 21+ event with a $5 door fee, doors are at 7PM and music starts at 8PM small-town lads... big metal chads! Kalopsya is a melodic-metal band from St. Peter, MN. With music consisting of catchy hooks, melodic lead-guitar runs, and harmonized guitar solos, Kalopsya has quickly gained a following and has also become well-respected within the metal scene for being...well...just genuinely nice dudes! In late 2019 (just before the Great Plague swept the world), a great hunger was stirring within the bowels of St. Peter, MN. In order to satiate this carnivorous desire, members of HeirAfire, Faulter, and Alation congregated within a dank basement. From within this basement, a pact was made to deliver the most melodious metal that Southern Minnesota has ever seen.
